cards.question: What does the abbreviation SSE stand for
options: Static system error
Standard source error
Static source error
cards.explain: SSE is the static source error.

cards.question: What is pitot pressure
options: The build-up of air pressure in a tube with its opening across the airstream
The build-up of air pressure in a tube with its opening facing the airstream
The actual atmospheric pressure in the air surrounding the aircraft
cards.explain: Pitot pressure builds up in a tube whose opening points into the airstream.

cards.question: Where is the pitot tube usually located on the aircraft
options: Near the tail, on the fin itself or below the rudder
Near the nose, on the wing leading edge or below the flaps
Near the nose, on the nose itself or below the cockpit
cards.explain: These are the three locations used.

cards.question: What does the pitot tube consist of and which pressure is present in it during the entire flight
options: A flapper plate chamber in which total pressure Ptot is present
A cylindrical pipe in which total pressure Ptot is present
A cylindrical pipe in which static pressure Ps is present
cards.explain: It is a cylindrical pipe carrying total pressure throughout the flight.

cards.question: Why is the Prandtl tube electrically heated
options: To prevent condensation
To prevent icing
To prevent deformation
cards.explain: Electrical heating keeps the probe free of ice.

cards.question: A Prandtl tube supplies both pressures from one probe. Where is it located on the aircraft?
options: At the rear of the aircraft
At the front of the aircraft
Under the wing of the aircraft
cards.explain: It sits at the front, like the pitot tube.

cards.question: What the altimeter and the vertical speed indicator have in common is that
options: Both use static pressure
Both use pitot pressure and static pressure
Both use pitot pressure
cards.explain: Static pressure is named as the pressure used by each of these two instruments.

cards.question: Compared with the simple system of a small aircraft, a modern commercial aircraft has
options: One pitot system feeding two static systems
One pitot system and one static system as well
Two or three separate pitot-static pressure systems
cards.explain: The simple system has one of each, whereas the modern commercial aircraft has two or three separate systems.

cards.question: On which two quantities does air pressure p depend
options: Temperature and angle of attack
Air density and mach number
Air density and temperature
cards.explain: Air density and temperature are the two quantities involved.

cards.question: Besides the mach number, which flight condition value is listed as a factor the static source error depends on
options: The angle of attack
The outside air temperature
The air density
cards.explain: Angle of attack is one of the factors the static source error depends on, alongside the mach number and the two configuration items.

cards.question: Why can a static source error arise on an aircraft
options: It is not always possible to calibrate the pneumatic devices to the ISA values
It is not always possible to find turbulence and ram air free zones on the aircraft
It is not always possible to keep the static ports electrically heated in flight
cards.explain: Where no turbulence free and ram air free zone exists, the sensed static pressure is falsified.

cards.question: How large is the static source error on slow-flying propeller planes
options: So small that it must be measured
So large that it must be corrected
So small that it is negligible
cards.explain: At low speed the error is negligible.

cards.question: The crew has to obtain the correct value from the distorted values being displayed. Where are the correction tables found?
options: In the Aircraft Maintenance Manual or in the flight log
In the Operating Manual or in the weight and balance data
In the Operating Manual or in the flight regulations
cards.explain: The correction tables come from the Operating Manual and from the flight regulations.

cards.question: Which pressure alone is required to measure the speed of the aircraft in relation to the ambient air
options: The total pressure Ptot
The static pressure ps
The ram pressure q
cards.explain: Only the dynamic or ram pressure q is needed for speed measurement.

cards.question: Which statement correctly compares the electrical heating of the pitot tube with that of the static ports
options: The pitot tube is heated, the static ports only on some aircraft types
Only the static ports are heated, the pitot tube being self draining
Both are heated on every aircraft type
cards.explain: Electrical heating is standard for the pitot tube, whereas electrically heated static ports are fitted on some aircraft types only.

cards.question: A pitot tube must be aligned in one particular direction when it is refitted because
options: the airstream keeps the pitot drain hole clear of water
pitot pressure builds up only in a tube facing the airstream
the airstream stops the pitot tube from freezing up
cards.explain: Pitot pressure only builds up when the opening of the tube faces the airstream, so the alignment is what produces the pressure.

cards.question: What do the small drain hole and the baffle of a pitot tube ensure
options: That ram air entering the tube is slowed down
That water entering the tube is drained away
That the tube inlet is kept free of any deformation
cards.explain: Their job is to get rid of water that has entered the tube.

cards.question: A student is worried that the drain hole in a pitot tube lets pressure escape. Which statement is correct?
options: The drain hole and the baffle slightly reduce the total pressure
The drain hole and the baffle do not affect the total pressure
The drain hole and the baffle slightly reduce the static pressure
cards.explain: The drain hole and baffle do not affect the total pressure.

cards.question: What does the Prandtl tube combine in one unit
options: A pitot tube with a sensor to measure static pressure
A pitot tube with a sensor to measure total air temperature
A static port with a sensor to measure the angle of attack
cards.explain: It puts the pitot function and a static pressure sensor into one probe.

cards.question: A Prandtl tube is found with a rough surface after a repair. Which consequence must be expected?
options: It will lead to static pressure errors
It will lead to heating element failures
It will lead to total pressure errors
cards.explain: Roughness disturbs the flow over the side holes and falsifies static pressure.

cards.question: A Prandtl tube delivers total pressure and static pressure. Where is the required differential pressure obtained?
options: In the instrument or in a computer
In the tube itself or in the piping
In the static port or in the drain hole
cards.explain: The subtraction is done in the instrument or in a computer, not in the probe.

cards.question: The pitot probe of a simple system becomes completely blocked while the static system stays clear. Which of the three supplied instruments is affected?
options: The altimeter
The airspeed indicator
The vertical speed indicator
cards.explain: Of the three instruments only the airspeed indicator uses pitot pressure, so only it depends on the pitot probe.

cards.question: During a repair the connection between the left and right hand measuring locations of one static pressure system is left open. What is lost by this?
options: The compensation for unbalance in pressure measurement
The heating of the static measuring locations
The supply of pitot pressure to the instruments
cards.explain: The two locations are joined only to compensate unbalance in pressure measurement, so breaking the joint removes that compensation.

cards.question: A technician traces one static pressure system of a small aeroplane and finds a measuring location on the left and on the right hand side of the fuselage. Which statement describes this arrangement correctly?
options: Both locations belong to the same pitot system and are connected together
Each location belongs to a separate static system and they stay isolated
Both locations belong to the same static system and are connected together
cards.explain: One static system uses both side locations and they are joined to each other.

cards.question: The Captain moves the handle of the alternate static source selector valve to its other position. Which static pressure then reaches his instruments?
options: The copilot's static pressure system
His own static pressure system
The pitot pressure of his own system
cards.explain: The valve exists so that the Captain can take his static pressure from the copilot's system instead of his own.

cards.question: A helicopter cannot keep its static ports in air that is free of rotor downwash. Which fitting deals with this?
options: A drain hole at each static port
Special cover plates at the static ports
Electrically heated static ports
cards.explain: The cover plates are fitted for exactly this purpose, to compensate the effects of the strong rotor downwash at the ports.

cards.question: After a skin repair the zone around a static port is left with a rough surface. What must be expected at that port?
options: Pressure distorting turbulences
A loss of the port heating
A blockage of the pressure pipe
cards.explain: The zone is required to be smooth precisely so that no pressure distorting turbulences occur, so a rough surface allows them.

cards.question: Why are static ports placed in areas with low turbulence and ram air distortion
options: Because turbulence and ram air distortion block the static pressure hoses
Because turbulence and ram air distortion overheat the static port zones
Because turbulence and ram air distortion falsify the static pressure reading
cards.explain: A port in a quiet zone senses the true static pressure, while turbulence and ram air distortion at the port falsify that reading.

cards.question: An aeroplane extends its flaps on the approach. Which reading can change as a result of this alone?
options: The static pressure reading
The angle of attack reading
The total air temperature reading
cards.explain: The static source error depends on the position of the flaps, and it is the static pressure reading that this error affects.

cards.question: Of the factors the static source error depends on, the two that change with the configuration of the aircraft are
options: The mach number and the angle of attack
The mach number and the position of the flaps
The flap position and the nose gear position
cards.explain: Flaps and nose gear are the two listed items that are set by the aircraft configuration, the other two being flight condition values.

cards.question: An aeroplane changes its angle of attack in cruise with everything else unchanged. Which measurement may be affected by this?
options: The total pressure measurement
The static pressure measurement
The pitot pressure measurement
cards.explain: The angle of attack is one of the factors the static source error depends on, and that error affects the static pressure reading.

cards.question: A slow-flying propeller plane and a jet aeroplane near the speed of sound differ above all in one of the static source error factors. Which factor is that?
options: The position of the flaps
The position of the nose gear
The mach number
cards.explain: The two cases are set apart by how near the speed of sound they fly, which is the mach number among the listed factors.

cards.question: A jet aeroplane flies near to the speed of sound and its static source error exceeds the tolerances required by law. Which correction becomes necessary?
options: A correction using an air data computer
A correction using a differential pressure bellows
A correction using an alternate static source valve
cards.explain: An air data computer correction is called for in this case.

cards.question: A static source error falsifies the static pressure supplied to a simple pitot-static system. Which instruments are affected?
options: Only the airspeed indicator of the system
Every instrument of the system
Only the vertical speed indicator of the system
cards.explain: All three instruments of the simple system are supplied with static pressure, so all three are affected.

cards.question: In the relation Ptot = q + ps, the quantity ps is delivered to the instrument from
options: The pitot probe
The static ports
The drain hole of the pitot tube
cards.explain: The static pressure ps used in the relation is the pressure measured at the static ports.

cards.question: An airspeed indicator is fed from the pitot probe as well as the static system because
options: The pitot probe cannot deliver a pressure without a static reference
The ram pressure it needs is the total pressure less the static pressure
The static pressure alone gives the speed in the surrounding air
cards.explain: Speed needs the ram pressure, and the ram pressure is obtained by subtracting the static pressure from the total pressure delivered by the pitot probe.

cards.question: A pitot tube delivers the pressure present in its cylindrical pipe throughout the flight. What must be supplied in addition before a speed can be obtained?
options: The static pressure from the static ports
A second total pressure from another pitot tube
The total air temperature from a temperature probe
cards.explain: The pitot tube gives total pressure only, and the static pressure from the static ports has to be subtracted from it to get the ram pressure.

cards.question: An aircraft type is to take both the ram pressure and the static pressure needed for speed indication from one single ram air tube. Which probe is used?
options: A pitot tube
A multi function probe
A Prandtl tube
cards.explain: The Prandtl tube is the single ram air tube that supplies both of these pressures.

cards.question: A Prandtl tube carries a feature that a plain pitot tube does not, namely
options: Holes drilled in the sides for the static lines
Electrical heating of the tube
A cylindrical inlet for the total pressure
cards.explain: Both probes have a cylindrical pipe and electrical heating, but the side holes feeding static lines belong to the Prandtl tube.

cards.question: Both a pitot tube and a Prandtl tube keep water out of the pitot line. Which item does this in the Prandtl tube together with the drain hole?
options: A baffle
A cover plate
A flapper plate
cards.explain: The Prandtl tube works with a flapper plate and a drain hole, the baffle being the item named for the pitot tube.

cards.question: A Prandtl tube delivers Ptot and Ps to a computer. Which quantity does the computer obtain from them, and what is it needed for?
options: The ram pressure, needed for the speed indication
The total air temperature, needed for the speed indication
The static source error, needed for the altitude indication
cards.explain: The differential of the two delivered pressures is the ram pressure q, which is what the speed indication requires.

cards.question: An air data system receives three parameters from one single multi function probe. Which parameters are they?
options: Angle of attack, total air temperature and total pressure
Angle of attack, static air temperature and static pressure
Angle of sideslip, total air temperature and total pressure
cards.explain: AOA, TAT and total pressure are the three outputs of the probe.

cards.question: Which part of the multi function probe measures the angle of attack
options: A TAT tube
A pitot probe
A wind vane
cards.explain: The wind vane is the AOA sensing element.

cards.question: Which colour is used to designate pitot system connections
options: Red
Blue
Yellow
cards.explain: Pitot connections carry the red designation; yellow belongs to the static side.

cards.question: Two lines are parted at a quick-disconnect during maintenance. What happens at the coupling?
options: It vents the line to ambient air
It seals itself automatically
It stays open until a cap is fitted
cards.explain: A self-sealing coupling closes the line itself the moment it is parted.

cards.question: A technician must check the mouth of a static port against its limits. Where are these limits normally found?
options: In ATA chapter 31
In ATA chapter 21
In ATA chapter 34
cards.explain: The limits for the static port mouth are given in ATA chapter 34.

cards.question: Which system controls the cabin rate
options: The anti-ice system
The airconditioning system
The pitot static system
cards.explain: The cabin rate is controlled by the airconditioning system.

cards.question: A multi function sensor must deliver the total pressure to the air data system. Which of its parts provides this parameter?
options: The temperature tube
The wind vane
The pitot probe
cards.explain: The built-in pitot probe supplies the total pressure.

cards.question: Each multi function probe has to pass its measured data to the related computer. Through which item does it do so?
options: Through the air data computer
Through the digital converter
Through the difference bellows
cards.explain: The digital converter is the link between the probe and the related computer.

cards.question: In some aircraft types the two pneumatic back up instruments are arranged so that
options: Both functions are integrated in one instrument
Both functions are shared between three instruments
Only the altitude function is retained
cards.explain: The two standby functions can be brought together in a single instrument on some types.

cards.question: An instrument has been changed in the pitot static system. What must be carried out?
options: An approved leak-proof test of the system
An approved flushing of the static system
An approved accuracy check of the static ports
cards.explain: Changing an instrument or a device calls for an approved leak-proof test.

cards.question: Why are a scale and a feeler-gage used at a static port
options: To check that the static port zone is smooth enough to prevent turbulences
To measure the mouth of the static port against the limits
To assess damage of the aircraft skin against the limits
cards.explain: The scale and feeler-gage are the tools named for assessing skin damage against the AMM limits.

cards.question: Why must the static port zones have a smooth surface
options: So that no turbulences can occur
So that no ice can form on the port
So that water can drain away from the port
cards.explain: A smooth zone keeps the airflow undisturbed so the port senses true static pressure.

cards.question: Where are the limits for damage of the skin at the static ports found
options: In the ATA chapter for the instruments or the IPC
In the ATA chapter for the aircraft structure or the SRM
In the ATA chapter for air conditioning or the wiring manual
cards.explain: Skin damage is a structural item, so the structure chapter or the SRM holds those limits.

cards.question: What do the results of a leakage depend on
options: The size of the leakage and the altitude of the aircraft
The size of the leakage and whether the cabin is pressurized
The position of the leakage and the outside air temperature
cards.explain: Size of the leak and the pressurization state of the cabin are the two factors given.

cards.question: A static line leaks inside the unpressurized cabin of an aircraft in flight. What does the altimeter do?
options: It freezes at the altitude flown when the leak started
It slightly decreases the indicated altitude
It slightly increases the indicated altitude
cards.explain: The lower cabin pressure reaching the static line reads as a slightly greater altitude.

cards.question: Which effect does a static system leakage inside an unpressurized cabin have on the airspeed indicator
options: It shows zero indicated airspeed
It shows a slightly higher indicated airspeed
It shows a slightly lower indicated airspeed
cards.explain: The airspeed indicator reads slightly high, in the same sense as the altimeter.

cards.question: What happens to the pressure in the static lines when a static system leakage goes into a pressurized cabin
options: The pressure increases
The pressure stays unchanged
The pressure decreases
cards.explain: Cabin pressure is above the ambient static pressure, so the static lines see a rise.

cards.question: What happens to the indications of the altimeter and the airspeed indicator after a static leakage into a pressurized cabin
options: Both increase
Both stay unchanged
Both decrease
cards.explain: The raised static pressure drives both indications down.

cards.question: An air data system is to receive the angle of attack and the total pressure from one single sensor. Which type is used?
options: A Prandtl tube
A pitot tube
A multi function probe
cards.explain: Only the multi function probe gives angle of attack as well as total pressure.

cards.question: A multi function probe delivers Ptot to the air data system, so the quantity still required for a speed indication is
options: The total air temperature
The angle of attack
The static pressure
cards.explain: The ram pressure needed for speed is the total pressure less the static pressure, and the probe supplies only the total pressure of the two.

cards.question: An aircraft with a modern EFIS carries two pneumatic back up instruments. Which of them has to be connected to the pitot system?
options: The standby altimeter
The standby airspeed indicator
Both of them equally
cards.explain: An airspeed indicator uses pitot pressure as well as static pressure, while an altimeter uses static pressure only.

cards.question: A line was parted only at a quick-disconnect. What applies to the leak-proof test?
options: It is required, but only on the static side
It is not required in this case
It is required, as after any other parting
cards.explain: A parting at a quick-disconnect is the one exception to the leak-proof test requirement.

cards.question: A static line breaks inside an unpressurized cabin during flight. How does the vertical speed indicator behave?
options: It slowly drifts into a permanent climb indication
It jumps once and then stays at zero
It jumps once and then shows correct data
cards.explain: The VSI reacts only to the sudden change and then works normally again.

cards.question: The same static line leak is considered in an unpressurized aircraft and in a pressurized one. How does the altimeter behave in each case?
options: It decreases the indication in the unpressurized aircraft and slightly increases it in the pressurized one
It slightly increases the indication in the unpressurized aircraft and decreases it in the pressurized one
It slightly increases the indication in both aircraft
cards.explain: With an unpressurized cabin the leak lowers the pressure in the static lines, so the altimeter reads slightly higher, while cabin pressure entering the lines of a pressurized aircraft raises that pressure, so it reads lower.

cards.question: Which behaviour does the vertical speed indicator show after a static system leakage in an unpressurized cabin compared with a pressurized cabin
options: An indication depending on cabin rate in the unpressurized cabin, and a small jump and then correct data in the pressurized cabin
A small jump and then correct data in both cabins
A small jump and then correct data in the unpressurized cabin, and an indication depending on cabin rate in the pressurized cabin
cards.explain: The unpressurized case gives a single small jump and then correct data, while in the pressurized aircraft the indication follows the cabin rate.

cards.question: The static system of a pressurized aircraft is leaking inside. What does the vertical speed indication now depend on?
options: The aircraft rate of climb
The size of the leak
The cabin rate
cards.explain: With cabin air in the static line the VSI follows the cabin rate, not the aircraft.

cards.question: Which instrument is affected by a leakage in the pitot system
options: The vertical speed indicator only
The airspeed indicator only
The altimeter only
cards.explain: Only the airspeed indicator is fed from the pitot system.

cards.question: What does a completely blocked pitot tube mean
options: The drain hole is blocked and the inlet is open
The inlet is blocked and the drain hole is open
The inlet and the drain hole are blocked
cards.explain: Complete blockage covers both the inlet and the drain hole.

cards.question: A pitot tube is completely blocked by ice. Which instruments are not affected?
options: The altimeter and the airspeed indicator
The altimeter and the vertical speed indicator
The airspeed indicator and the vertical speed indicator
cards.explain: Those two run on static pressure, which the pitot blockage does not touch.

cards.question: The indications fluctuate during a check of the pitot static system. What does this show?
options: The presence of water in the pressure pipes
The presence of ice at the static port
The presence of a leak in the pressure pipes
cards.explain: Fluctuating indications are the sign of water lying in the pipes.

cards.question: A pitot line leaks inside an unpressurized cabin. What does the airspeed indication do?
options: It increases into the overspeed region
It decreases until it reaches zero
It stays at the value flown when the leak started
cards.explain: With the pitot line open to the cabin the airspeed indication falls away to zero.

cards.question: Why does the airspeed indication decrease when both the pitot and the static system leak
options: The total pressure in the pitot line is trapped at a constant value
Pitot and static pressure in the lines tend to be the same
The static pressure in the lines rises above the pitot pressure
cards.explain: Both lines fill with the same cabin pressure, so the difference the indicator works on shrinks.

cards.question: Both the pitot system and the static system are leaking. What do the altimeter and the vertical speed indicator show?
options: The same results as for a leakage in the pitot system
The same results as for a leakage in the static system
Correct indications, because the two leaks cancel each other
cards.explain: Those two instruments see only static pressure, so the static leak result still applies.

cards.question: What happens to the indications with a blocked static system while the aircraft flies at constant altitude and constant airspeed
options: The airspeed indication slowly decreases
The altitude indication slowly increases
There are no changes in the indication
cards.explain: Nothing changes while the trapped static pressure still matches the real one.

cards.question: Which indications do the altimeter and the vertical speed indicator give with a blocked static system, during a climb and during a descent
options: The same altitude and a vertical speed that follows the aircraft
A changing altitude and a vertical speed of zero
The same altitude and a vertical speed of zero
cards.explain: Both instruments work from the trapped static pressure, so the altitude stays frozen and the vertical speed stays at zero in the climb and in the descent alike.

cards.question: Why does the airspeed indicator react like an altimeter when the pitot tube is totally blocked
options: The total pressure is trapped, so only the changing static pressure moves the indication
Total and static pressure become nearly equal, so the indication falls away
The static pressure is trapped, so only the changing total pressure moves the indication
cards.explain: With the total pressure held fixed the indication is driven only by static pressure, which is what an altimeter responds to.

cards.question: What happens to the pitot pressure when the pitot tube inlet is blocked but the water drain hole is still open
options: It decreases to the value of the static pressure
It increases to the value of the total pressure
It stays at the value it had before the blockage
cards.explain: The open drain lets the trapped pressure bleed down to static.

cards.question: Why are the altimeter and the vertical speed indicator not affected by a blocked pitot inlet
options: They get both pitot and static pressure
They only get pitot pressure
They only get static pressure
cards.explain: Both instruments are fed from the static system alone.

cards.question: Why can water be present in the pressure pipes
options: Their test fittings are used to simulate altitude and speed
They are not drained on a regular basis
They are capped for protection during testing
cards.explain: The pipes are not drained routinely, so water can collect in them.

cards.question: The static ports of a cold aeroplane are capped and the aircraft is moved into a warm hangar. What happens in the static system?
options: The pressure decreases
The pressure stays the same
The pressure increases
cards.explain: Warming the trapped air in a sealed static system raises its pressure.

cards.question: What can be said about the ram pressure when both the pitot inlet and the drain are iced over
options: It is always zero
It depends on the altitude
It is constant at every altitude
cards.explain: With the total pressure held fixed, only the static pressure varies, so ram pressure follows altitude.

cards.question: Why does the airspeed indication fall to zero with a pitot leakage in an unpressurized cabin
options: Static and pitot pressure become nearly the same
The pitot pressure rises with the cabin pressure
The static pressure becomes much greater than the pitot pressure
cards.explain: The airspeed indicator works on the difference between the two pressures, which is now almost nil.

cards.question: A pitot line leaks inside a pressurized cabin. What can be said about the airspeed indication?
options: It always falls to zero, because pitot and static pressure become equal
It always rises, because the cabin pressure is higher than the static pressure
It is unpredictable, because it depends on altitude and cabin pressure
cards.explain: With a pressurized cabin the two varying pressures make the indication unpredictable.

cards.question: Which instruments are disturbed by a leakage in the pitot system alone, compared with a leakage in both the pitot and the static system
options: All three instruments, compared with the airspeed indicator alone
The airspeed indicator and the altimeter, compared with all three instruments
Only the airspeed indicator, compared with all three instruments
cards.explain: A leak in the pitot system alone affects the airspeed indicator only; once the static system leaks as well, the altimeter and the vertical speed indication are disturbed too.

cards.question: Both the pitot system and the static system leak inside an unpressurized cabin. What does the altimeter do?
options: It slightly increases the indicated altitude
It holds the altitude it had when the leakage started
It slightly decreases the indicated altitude
cards.explain: With both systems leaking the altimeter shows the same result as for a static leak, and in an unpressurized cabin that result is a slightly increased indicated altitude.

cards.question: An aircraft cruises at constant altitude and constant airspeed with a blocked static system and then begins a climb. What does the altimeter do?
options: It increases its altitude indication as the climb starts
It continues to display the same altitude
It jumps once and then follows the climb correctly
cards.explain: The trapped static pressure cannot change, so the altimeter holds the same altitude in level flight and through the climb.

cards.question: Why does the airspeed indication decrease during a climb with a blocked static system
options: The total pressure falls while the trapped static pressure stays constant
The total pressure and the static pressure both decrease together
The total pressure from the pitot tube stays constant while the static pressure decreases
cards.explain: Only the total pressure falls; the blocked static side cannot follow it.

cards.question: How does the airspeed indication behave with a blocked static system during a climb compared with a descent
options: Decreasing during both the climb and the descent
Increasing during the climb and decreasing during the descent
Decreasing during the climb and increasing during the descent
cards.explain: The trapped static pressure stays fixed while the total pressure falls in the climb and rises in the descent, so the indication first decreases and then increases.

cards.question: Why does the airspeed indication increase during a descent with a blocked static system
options: The total pressure and the static pressure both increase together
The total pressure rises while the trapped static pressure stays constant
The trapped static pressure increases while the total pressure remains constant
cards.explain: Only the total pressure rises; the blocked static side stays where it was.

cards.question: Two aircraft climb, one with a blocked static system and one with a completely blocked pitot tube. What does the airspeed indicator show in each?
options: A decreasing indication in both aircraft
A decreasing indication with the blocked static system and an increasing indication with the blocked pitot tube
An increasing indication with the blocked static system and a decreasing indication with the blocked pitot tube
cards.explain: With the static side blocked the climb gives a decreasing indication, while with the pitot side blocked the total pressure is trapped and the falling static pressure drives the indication up.

cards.question: How does the airspeed indication behave during a descent with a blocked static system compared with a completely blocked pitot tube
options: Decreasing with the blocked static system and increasing with the blocked pitot tube
Increasing with the blocked static system and decreasing with the blocked pitot tube
Increasing with both blockages
cards.explain: With the static side blocked the descent gives an increasing indication, while with the pitot side blocked the total pressure is trapped and the rising static pressure drives the indication down.

cards.question: The pitot tube becomes totally blocked in cruise and the thrust is then increased to accelerate. What does the airspeed indicator show?
options: A rise in the indicated speed
A fall of the indicated speed to zero
No change in the indicated speed
cards.explain: At constant altitude neither pressure changes, so the reading is frozen whatever the thrust.

cards.question: The pitot inlet of an aircraft is found blocked by ice. Which indication shows that the water drain hole is still open?
options: The airspeed indication increases into the overspeed region
The airspeed indication stops responding to changes of thrust
The airspeed indication decreases all the way to zero
cards.explain: With the drain open the pitot pressure falls to static and the indication drops to zero, which a completely blocked tube does not do.

cards.question: What happens to the pitot pressure and the airspeed indication when the pitot inlet is iced over but the drain is free
options: The pitot pressure remains constant and the airspeed indication decreases to zero
The pitot pressure falls to static pressure and the airspeed indication increases
The pitot pressure falls to static pressure and the airspeed indication decreases to zero
cards.explain: The open drain lets the pitot pressure fall to static pressure, leaving no difference for the indicator to show.

cards.question: The pitot inlet is iced over but the drain is free. What does this tell you about the heating?
options: The heating is defective or deactivated
The heating is working correctly
The heating is insufficient
cards.explain: Ice only at the inlet points to heating that is working but not enough.

cards.question: Both the pitot inlet and the drain are iced over. What does this say about the heating and the pitot pressure?
options: The heating is defective or deactivated and the pitot pressure remains constant
The heating is defective or deactivated and the pitot pressure falls to static pressure
The heating is insufficient and the pitot pressure falls to static pressure
cards.explain: Complete icing means the heating has failed or is off, and the sealed pitot pressure cannot change.

questions.question: One of the factors on which the choice of altimeter depends is
options: The number of static ports fitted
The transition level at the destination
The tolerance values required by law
questions.explain: Legal tolerance values are one of the three listed selection factors.

questions.question: Besides the double pointer, triple pointer and drum-type instruments, altitude is also indicated
options: on the PFD
on the transponder
on the baro scale
questions.explain: The fourth kind of indication listed is the altitude display on the PFD.

questions.question: The shape of the ISA pressure graph at low altitudes is
options: Strongly exponential
A series of steps
Nearly linear
questions.explain: Close to the ground the pressure against altitude curve is nearly a straight line.

questions.question: An aircraft climbs. What happens inside its barometric altimeter?
options: Pressure increases, the bellows expand and the pointer falls
Pressure decreases, the bellows contract and the pointer rises
Pressure decreases, the bellows expand and the pointer rises
questions.explain: Falling pressure around the capsule lets the bellows expand, which drives the pointer up the scale.

questions.question: An encoding altimeter puts out an ALT signal. Which system receives it?
options: The air data computer
The static system
The ATC transponder system
questions.explain: The encoding altimeter feeds the ALT signal to the ATC transponder.

questions.question: Why do pilots of medium and large aircraft normally not use QFE?
options: They can use a radio altimeter system
Their baro scales cannot be set that low
The QFE value is not transmitted by data link
questions.explain: A radio altimeter already gives the height above the ground, so the QFE setting is not needed.

questions.question: VNE is
options: The maximum allowed airspeed
The maximum allowable speed with flaps extended
The maximum airspeed for cruise flight
questions.explain: VNE is the never exceed speed, which is the maximum allowed airspeed.

questions.question: On a helicopter airspeed indicator the red-white mark shows
options: The range of transition lift
The maximum speed allowed for autorotation
The speed that must never be exceeded
questions.explain: The red-white mark is the autorotation speed limit.

questions.question: A technician traces the pitot line to the airspeed indicator capsule. Which pressure does that line deliver to the capsule interior?
options: Dynamic pressure from the static system
Total pressure from the pitot system
Static pressure from the static system
questions.explain: The capsule interior receives total pressure, which the pitot system delivers.

questions.question: TAS is obtained from IAS by correcting for instrument error, static source error, dynamic pressure error and
options: Aircraft weight
Air density
Magnetic variation
questions.explain: Air density is the fourth correction listed for deriving TAS from IAS.

questions.question: From which pressures is the indicated mach number Mi calculated
options: Dynamic pressure and cabin pressure
Pitot pressure and accumulator pressure
Pitot pressure and dynamic pressure
questions.explain: Mi, the indicated mach number, is calculated from pitot pressure and dynamic pressure.

questions.question: A machmeter is opened and found to contain a differential pressure bellows and an aneroid bellows. Which instruments use these same two sensing elements?
options: The airspeed indicator uses a differential pressure capsule and the vertical speed indicator an aneroid capsule
The airspeed indicator uses a differential pressure capsule and the altimeter an aneroid capsule
The altimeter uses a differential pressure capsule and the airspeed indicator an aneroid capsule
questions.explain: The airspeed indicator measures with a differential pressure capsule and the altimeter with an aneroid capsule, and a mach meter contains both of those bellows.

questions.question: A jet aeroplane in high altitude cruise triggers its overspeed warning. Which limit has been exceeded, and does the warning depend on the airspeed indication?
options: MMO, and the detection is independent of the airspeed indication
MMO, and the detection is taken from the airspeed indication
VMO, and the detection is independent of the airspeed indication
questions.explain: At higher altitudes the limit depends on the maximum allowed Mach number, MMO, and the overspeed detection is always independent of the airspeed indication.

questions.question: Why is a vertical speed indicator connected to the static system only
options: Because it works from the difference between total pressure and static pressure
Because it works from changes of static pressure acting on its bellows
Because it works from the delay of the total pressure through a capillary
questions.explain: The instrument senses air pressure changes with static pressure on both sides of its bellows, so it needs no pitot connection.

questions.question: How is pressure balanced out in a diaphragm variometer
options: Via the air gap between the diaphragm and the casing
Via a capillary tube between the diaphragm and the casing
Via a calibrated orifice in the centre of the diaphragm
questions.explain: Balancing takes place through the air gap between diaphragm and casing.

questions.question: The airspeed value that the temperature display is used to determine is
options: TAS
EAS
IAS
questions.explain: The temperature display is used among other things for determining the TAS.

questions.question: The engine related use of the temperature display is
options: Calculating engine vibration and determining balance limits
Calculating engine oil quantity and determining oil limits
Calculating engine performance and determining engine limits
questions.explain: Air temperature feeds engine performance calculation and the engine limits.

questions.question: A flush skin probe supplies temperature in the RAT form. Why can that reading not be used as the ambient air temperature?
options: RAT is deflected around the fuselage, so it reads lower than the ambient SAT
RAT is taken downstream of the probe heater, so it reads higher than the ambient SAT
RAT still contains part of the ram rise, so it reads higher than the ambient SAT
questions.explain: RAT sits between TAT and SAT, so it is still above ambient and the SAT has to be calculated.

questions.question: In cruise the crew needs the static air temperature. How is that value produced?
options: It is calculated from the TAT and the mach number in the air data computer
It is read directly from a second, unheated static temperature probe
It is read directly from the ram air temperature indicator
questions.explain: SAT cannot be sensed directly, so the ADC derives it from the measured TAT and the mach number.

questions.question: An aeroplane stands in strong sunshine and its skin is hot. Which probe design keeps these conditions out of the temperature reading, and how?
options: An aspirated TAT probe, because compressed air blown backwards carries outside air along
A standard TAT probe, because its heating element masks the effect of the sun
A flush skin probe, because the skin and the probe then settle at the same temperature
questions.explain: The aspirated probe keeps outside air moving through it, so sun and skin temperature on the ground can be ignored.

questions.question: An aircraft makes only small changes of height. What happens to the coarse synchro value in the electrical altimeter?
options: It is blocked by the OFF flag monitor
It is blocked by the HIGH LEVEL detector
It is blocked by the LIMITER
questions.explain: For small height changes the fine value alone is used and the HIGH LEVEL detector blocks the coarse value.

questions.question: A glass cockpit aircraft displays calibrated airspeed. What has been corrected to obtain it?
options: The error from the indicator and the error from the static pressure source
The error from the pitot source and the error from the air density
The error from the indicator and the error from the compressibility of the air
questions.explain: CAS is IAS corrected for instrument error and static source error.

questions.question: An aircraft is fitted with two air data computers. How are their pressure sources arranged?
options: Both computers are fed from the standby pitot and static system
Both computers are fed from one common pitot and static system
Each computer has its own separated pitot and static system
questions.explain: Each of the two computers is given a separate pitot and static system of its own.

questions.question: The static pressure reaching an analogue air data computer is in error. What is the effect of this on the Mach indication
options: The Mach number stays correct, because the Mach module has a pressure input of its own
The Mach number is wrong as well, because the Mach module works from the temperature input
The Mach number is wrong as well, because the Mach module works from the other two modules
questions.explain: The Mach module takes its information from the altitude and airspeed modules, both of which use the static pressure, so an error in that pressure carries into the Mach number.

questions.question: A servo corrected altimeter reads several thousand feet away from the altitude sent by the air data computer. Why does the correction not bring it into agreement?
options: Correction only works above the altitude set on the baro scale
Correction is inhibited while the internal vibrator is running
Correction is only possible within a few hundred feet
questions.explain: Continuous correction requires the error voltage to be about zero, which limits it to a few hundred feet.

questions.question: A red flag shows against one parameter on a Mach/airspeed indicator while the other parameter reads normally. What should the engineer conclude?
options: The fault may lie in the air data computer or in the indicator
The fault must lie in the pitot and static system
The fault must lie in the air data computer itself
questions.explain: The indicator raises the same flag for its own internal faults, so the flag alone does not isolate the computer.

questions.question: An aircraft climbs while holding a constant equivalent airspeed. What happens to the true airspeed?
options: It stays the same, because the two values are identical at every altitude
It decreases, because the true airspeed falls with increasing altitude
It increases, because the true airspeed rises with increasing altitude
questions.explain: For a given EAS the TAS increases with increasing altitude, and is identical to the EAS only at mean sea level.

questions.question: An analogue air data computer is unserviceable and a DADC is offered as a replacement. What applies?
options: The DADC may not be installed in place of an analogue computer
The DADC may be installed in place of the analogue computer
The DADC may only be installed if both computers are changed together
questions.explain: The replacement is allowed in that direction only, because the DADC also provides analogue outputs.

questions.question: A digital air data computer has lost its angle of attack, flap and gear position inputs. Which of its functions is degraded?
options: The data corrections, such as the static source error correction
The conversion of the input pressures into electrical signals
The transmission of the computed values on the output busses
questions.explain: Those inputs are used for the data corrections, so only the correction accuracy suffers.

questions.question: The air data computers have failed, yet the digital vertical speed indicator still gives a usable indication. Why?
options: It normally works from the vertical speed output of the air data computer
It normally works from the static pressure rate measured in the indicator itself
It normally works from the inertial vertical speed signal of the inertial reference unit
questions.explain: The normal source is the IRU, so the indication survives the loss of the air data computers.

questions.question: The altitude shown on the primary flight displays disagrees with the standby instrument. Which settings should be compared?
options: The baro correction on the EFIS control panel and the air data source selection
The baro correction on the EFIS control panel and the BARO setting on the standby instrument
The BARO setting on the standby instrument and the selected altitude on the mode control panel
questions.explain: The baro correction for the primary flight displays is selected at the EFIS control panel, while the standby instrument has its own BARO rotary knob, so the two references are set separately and a disagreement points to the two settings being different.

questions.question: A student looks for the Mach number on the navigation display and cannot find it. Why not?
options: Mach number is only shown when the autopilot is engaged
True airspeed is the only air data indication on that display
Mach number is only shown above the Mach changeover altitude
questions.explain: The ND carries TAS alone; the rest of the air data, Mach included, is on the primary flight display.

questions.question: An air data module at a pitot probe has converted the pressure it senses. Which path does the resulting signal then follow?
options: To an air data inertial reference unit, and from there on to the user systems
To the display management computers, and from there on to an air data inertial reference unit
To the standby instruments, and from there on to an air data inertial reference unit
questions.explain: The module feeds the ADIRU, which is the computer that produces the air data outputs for the displays and other systems.

questions.question: The antenna connection to the GPS part of a GNADIRU is broken. Which function of the box is lost, and which data stops reaching the flight management system?
options: The inertial reference function, and the present position it calculates
The GPS receiver function, and the present position it calculates
The GPS receiver function, and the barometric altitude it calculates
questions.explain: The GPS receiver needs the antenna to receive the satellite signals, so without it the present position it calculates and sends to the flight management system is lost.

questions.question: An integrated standby instrument system fails completely. Which standby indications are lost?
options: Standby altitude, standby attitude and standby airspeed
Standby altitude, standby airspeed and standby vertical speed
Standby altitude, standby attitude and standby heading
questions.explain: One unit does the work of the three separate standby instruments, so all three indications go together.

questions.question: The relationship between angle of attack and the lift acting on the wings is that
options: the greater the angle of attack, the smaller the lift
the greater the angle of attack, the greater the lift
the lift is independent of the angle of attack
questions.explain: Lift rises with angle of attack, up to the individual maximum for the profile.

questions.question: The wind vane type of angle of attack sensor is made force-free by
options: a spring, so that it returns to the neutral position on the ground
counterweights, so that it is articulated and free to take any position
a damper, so that it is held still while the aircraft is on the ground
questions.explain: Counterweights balance the vane so nothing but the airflow moves it.

questions.question: An aeroplane slows down in level flight with the slats and flaps left retracted. What happens to the angle of attack indication?
options: It decreases, because less lift is being produced at the lower speed
It stays constant, because the lift in level flight does not change
It increases, and approaches alpha max as the speed falls
questions.explain: With the wing geometry unchanged, holding the lift at a lower airspeed demands a larger angle of attack, which moves the indication toward alpha max.

questions.question: In flight the maximum possible angle of attack for the flap position in use is exceeded. What happens?
options: An amber lamp illuminates and a chime sounds
A motor shakes the control column
The flaps extend automatically
questions.explain: Exceeding the flap dependent maximum angle drives the stick shaker motor.

questions.question: An aeroplane is on its take-off roll at 50 kts with the pitch attitude unchanged. Is the stall warning management computer system active?
options: No, it is active only above 140 kts or above 5 deg of pitch angle
Yes, it is active above 40 kts whatever the pitch angle of the aircraft
Yes, it is active from the start of the take-off roll until touchdown
questions.explain: The system becomes active above 140 kts or above 5 deg of pitch angle and is switched off below 40 kts; at 50 kts with the pitch unchanged neither activation condition is met, so it is not yet active.

cards.question: The quantity measured by a radio altimeter is
options: The delay of a reflected wave
Gravitation model deviation
Static air pressure
cards.explain: The radio altimeter works on the delay of the radio wave, not on pressure.

cards.question: One of the factors on which the choice of altimeter depends is
options: The tolerance values required by law
The transition level at the destination
The number of static ports fitted
cards.explain: Legal tolerance values are one of the three listed selection factors.

cards.question: Besides the double pointer, triple pointer and drum-type instruments, altitude is also indicated
options: on the baro scale
on the transponder
on the PFD
cards.explain: The fourth kind of indication listed is the altitude display on the PFD.

cards.question: The shape of the ISA pressure graph at low altitudes is
options: Strongly exponential
A series of steps
Nearly linear
cards.explain: Close to the ground the pressure against altitude curve is nearly a straight line.

cards.question: The pressure decrease that corresponds to an altitude increase of 30 ft at low altitude is
options: 10 hPa
30 hPa
1 hPa
cards.explain: At low altitude the relationship is 30 ft per 1 hPa.

cards.question: What does the baro set knob give the altimeter
options: A new scale calibration in metres
A new static pressure source
A new reference pressure
cards.explain: The knob only changes the reference pressure the indication is based on.

cards.question: The crew is preparing for departure. Which pressure do they set on the altimeters?
options: The actual pressure related to sea level
The actual pressure at ground level
The standard pressure of the ISA
cards.explain: Before takeoff the reference is the actual sea level pressure, which is the QNH setting.

cards.question: The name given to the reference pressure used for QNE is
options: Standard
Ambient
Nautical
cards.explain: QNE uses the standard atmosphere with 1013 hPa as a reference, and that pressure is called standard.

cards.question: Who may select the barometric correction on an altimeter, besides the pilots
options: Air traffic control
Maintenance personnel
The air data computer
cards.explain: The baro correction is selected by the pilots or by maintenance personnel.

cards.question: How does a barometer determine altitude
options: By using the delay of a reflected radio wave
By using the increase in pressure with increasing altitude
By using the decrease in pressure with increasing altitude
cards.explain: Pressure falls as altitude rises, and the barometer uses that relationship.

cards.question: A method of determining altitude uses the WGS84 gravitation model as its reference instead of the ground. Which method is it?
options: GPS
Barometer
Radio altimeter
cards.explain: WGS84 is the reference of the GPS method; the barometer uses pressure and the radio altimeter uses the ground.

cards.question: How is the interior of a barometric altimeter casing connected
options: To the outside air via the static system
To the outside air via the pitot system
To a sealed reference vacuum
cards.explain: Outside air reaches the inside of the case through the static system.

cards.question: An aircraft climbs. What happens inside its barometric altimeter?
options: Pressure decreases, the bellows contract and the pointer rises
Pressure decreases, the bellows expand and the pointer rises
Pressure increases, the bellows expand and the pointer falls
cards.explain: Falling pressure around the capsule lets the bellows expand, which drives the pointer up the scale.

cards.question: The reason for mounting 2 or 3 bellows in series in an altimeter is
options: To allow the case to be sealed against static pressure
To balance the mechanism against acceleration
To obtain a more exact indication
cards.explain: Several capsules in series give more movement and therefore a more exact indication.

cards.question: An altitude indicator has no pneumatic connection at all, only wiring. Which type of instrument is it?
options: An indicator with electrical input from an air data computer
An instrument with static pressure input
A drum-type instrument with static pressure input
cards.explain: Without a static connection the altitude information can only come electrically from an air data computer.

cards.question: The construction feature that distinguishes an encoding altimeter is
options: An additional static port and a drum
Additional bellows and electrical connectors
Additional pointers and a second baro scale
cards.explain: The encoding altimeter carries extra bellows and electrical connectors on top of the normal altimeter.

cards.question: An encoding altimeter puts out an ALT signal. Which system receives it?
options: The static system
The air data computer
The ATC transponder system
cards.explain: The encoding altimeter feeds the ALT signal to the ATC transponder.

cards.question: Why is an encoding altimeter connected to the ATC transponder system?
options: So that the crew can be informed about the ground pressure
So that the transponder can set the baro correction of the altimeter
So that ground control can be informed about the altitude of the aircraft
cards.explain: The purpose of the ALT signal is to pass the aircraft altitude to ground control.

cards.question: Encoding altimeters are found in
options: some small aircraft
all aircraft fitted with an air data computer
only aircraft without a transponder
cards.explain: The encoding altimeter is described as a fit found in some small aircraft.

cards.question: How does the baro set knob work in a pneumatic indicator
options: It sends a correction signal to the air data computer
It moves the bellows stack alone
It directly turns the whole altimeter mechanism
cards.explain: In a pneumatic instrument the setting is made mechanically by turning the whole mechanism.

cards.question: A new reference pressure is selected on an electrical altitude indicator. How is the correction made?
options: Electrically inside the indicator or via an air data computer
Mechanically, by turning the whole altimeter mechanism
Pneumatically, by an additional set of bellows
cards.explain: Electrical indicators have no mechanism to turn, so the correction is done electrically.

cards.question: An aeroplane is parked at an aerodrome of considerable elevation, with QNH set on the altimeter. What does the instrument show?
options: The altitude of the airport related to mean sea level
The height of the aircraft above the runway
Zero feet
cards.explain: With sea level as the reference, an airport above sea level indicates its own elevation.

cards.question: The baro correction that makes the altimeter read zero on the ground is
options: QNH
QFE
QNE
cards.explain: QFE uses the ambient pressure at ground level, so the indication on the ground is zero.

cards.question: The pressure used for QFE is related to
options: ground level
mean sea level
the standard atmosphere
cards.explain: QFE is the ambient pressure at ground level, unlike QNH which is related to mean sea level.

cards.question: An aircraft is in flight with QFE set on its altimeter. What does the indication represent?
options: The height above mean sea level
The altitude in the standard atmosphere
The height above the ground
cards.explain: With the ground as reference the instrument shows height above the ground.

cards.question: Why do pilots of medium and large aircraft normally not use QFE?
options: Their baro scales cannot be set that low
They can use a radio altimeter system
The QFE value is not transmitted by data link
cards.explain: A radio altimeter already gives the height above the ground, so the QFE setting is not needed.

cards.question: An aircraft in flight has the baro correction for QNH set. What does the altimeter read?
options: The height above the transition altitude
The height above the ground
The height above mean sea level
cards.explain: QNH refers everything to mean sea level, in flight as well as on the ground.

cards.question: A technician selects QNE on an altimeter. Which reference is then used?
options: The ambient pressure at the airport
The standard atmosphere with 1013 hPa
The ambient pressure at mean sea level on the day
cards.explain: QNE is always the fixed standard atmosphere value, not a value measured on the day.

cards.question: Where is the QNE setting normally used
options: During takeoff and landing only
In flight, not on the ground
On the ground, not in flight
cards.explain: QNE is the in-flight setting; on the ground the airport settings are used.

cards.question: The advantage of QNE is that
options: all aircraft in cruise flight use the same reference pressure
the altimeter reads zero at touchdown
every aircraft reads its own height above the ground
cards.explain: The whole point of QNE is a single common reference for all aircraft in the cruise.

cards.question: An altimeter is set to standard pressure. Under which condition is its indicated altitude equal to the true altitude?
options: When the airport elevation is zero
When the pressure at sea level is really 1013 hPa
When the aircraft is above the transition altitude
cards.explain: The conversion from static pressure to altitude only matches the true altitude when the real sea level pressure is the calibration value.

cards.question: Why do all aircraft in cruise use one common selected pressure instead of the local pressure?
options: So that they all keep the same altitude separation in every pressure area
So that each of them indicates its true height above the ground
So that ground control can read the elevation of the airports
cards.explain: A common reference keeps the vertical separation between aircraft consistent whatever the local pressure is.

cards.question: An altimeter is left calibrated to 1013 hPa while the real pressure at sea level below the aircraft is lower. What will the instrument indicate?
options: Too high an altitude
The correct altitude
Too low an altitude
cards.explain: With the reference set higher than the real sea level pressure, the instrument over-reads.

cards.question: An aircraft passes the Transition Altitude after takeoff and later the Transition Level before landing. Which setting is made at each point?
options: The actual pressure at the departure airport at the Transition Altitude and 1013 hPa at the Transition Level
1013 hPa at the Transition Altitude and the actual pressure at the destination airport at the Transition Level
1013 hPa at both the Transition Altitude and the Transition Level
cards.explain: The common standard pressure is taken at the Transition Altitude on the way up and given back for the local pressure at the Transition Level on the way down.

cards.question: As a measuring instrument, the airspeed indicator is
options: A differential pressure meter
An absolute pressure meter
A differential temperature meter
cards.explain: The instrument works on the difference between two pressures, so it is a differential pressure meter.

cards.question: The scale of the airspeed indicator is calibrated in
options: Kilometres per hour
Knots
Nautical miles
cards.explain: The scale of the airspeed indicator is given in knots.

cards.question: VNE is
options: The maximum airspeed for cruise flight
The maximum allowable speed with flaps extended
The maximum allowed airspeed
cards.explain: VNE is the never exceed speed, which is the maximum allowed airspeed.

cards.question: The green band on the airspeed indicator of a small aircraft shows the
options: Full Flap Operating Range
Caution range
Normal Operating Range
cards.explain: Green marks the normal operating range on the scale.

cards.question: On a helicopter airspeed indicator the red mark shows
options: The range of transition lift
The speed that must never be exceeded
The maximum speed allowed for autorotation
cards.explain: Red marks VNE, the never exceed speed.

cards.question: On a helicopter airspeed indicator the red-white mark shows
options: The maximum speed allowed for autorotation
The speed that must never be exceeded
The range of transition lift
cards.explain: The red-white mark is the autorotation speed limit.

cards.question: True airspeed is the speed with which the aircraft moves
options: Relative to the airspeed indicator scale
Over the ground
Through the surrounding air
cards.explain: TAS is defined as the aircraft speed through the surrounding air mass.

cards.question: The speed which is shown on the indicator is called
options: Indicated airspeed
True airspeed
Ground speed
cards.explain: What the instrument displays is the indicated airspeed.

cards.question: A technician traces the pitot line to the airspeed indicator capsule. Which pressure does that line deliver to the capsule interior?
options: Static pressure from the static system
Dynamic pressure from the static system
Total pressure from the pitot system
cards.explain: The capsule interior receives total pressure, which the pitot system delivers.

cards.question: The capsule of an airspeed indicator sits inside a sealed casing. Which pressure acts inside that casing?
options: Static pressure from the static system
Total pressure from the pitot system
Dynamic pressure from the pitot system
cards.explain: The casing is fed from the static system, so static pressure surrounds the capsule.

cards.question: In an airspeed indicator the difference between total pressure and static pressure gives
options: Total pressure
Dynamic pressure
Static pressure
cards.explain: Total pressure minus static pressure is by definition the dynamic pressure.

cards.question: A technician is asked what the indicated airspeed value is used for. Which answer is correct?
options: As a value for lift and for the maximum load on the flaps
As a value for altitude and for the maximum rate of climb
As a value for thrust and for the maximum cabin pressure
cards.explain: Lift and the maximum load on the flaps and the airframe are among the uses of the IAS.

cards.question: An aircraft is fitted with a primary flight display instead of a mechanical airspeed indicator. How is airspeed presented?
options: As a speed bug on the PFD
As a speed limit marking on the PFD
As a speed band on the PFD
cards.explain: The third type of airspeed indication listed is the speed band shown on the PFD.

cards.question: In small aircraft the airspeed limits are shown by
options: A movable pointer driven by the air data computer
A digital readout beside the airspeed indicator
Coloured ranges and lines on the airspeed indicator scale
cards.explain: Small aircraft carry the limits as colour markings painted on the instrument scale.

cards.question: An aeroplane is being flown with the airspeed in the yellow band. Which condition applies?
options: It may only be used in smooth air without hard manoeuvres
It may only be used with the flaps extended
It may be used in any air, including hard manoeuvres
cards.explain: The caution range is restricted to smooth air with no hard manoeuvres.

cards.question: The slight increase of VMO with altitude is the result of taking account of
options: The compressibility error of the IAS
The instrument error of the IAS
The static source error of the IAS
cards.explain: The slight rise comes from the compressibility error of the IAS being taken into account.

cards.question: Airspeed indicators of jet aircraft do not show the low speed limit because
options: It is already shown by the maximum speed pointer
It is a fixed value and therefore needs no indication
It depends on many factors such as weight and flap position
cards.explain: The low speed limit varies with weight and flap position, so it is not marked on the dial.

cards.question: A crew wants a minimum speed indication in the cockpit. On which aircraft is it available, and where is it shown?
options: Only on piston engine aircraft, as a red line on the airspeed indicator
On all jet aircraft, as a coloured band on the airspeed indicator scale
Only on aircraft with a glass cockpit, on the speed tape of the PFD
cards.explain: The minimum speed indication is a glass cockpit feature shown on the PFD speed tape.

cards.question: A helicopter airspeed indicator carries two essential marked limits. What makes them necessary?
options: The aerodynamic properties of the helicopter
The maximum take-off weight of the helicopter
The engine power limits of the helicopter
cards.explain: The aerodynamic properties of the helicopter are the reason for the two limits marked on the airspeed indicator.

cards.question: An aircraft is flown at sea level in standard conditions and its IAS equals its TAS. Which further condition must be met?
options: With negligible compressibility error
With negligible static source error
With negligible instrument error
cards.explain: IAS and TAS coincide only at standard conditions at sea level and with a negligible static source error.

cards.question: TAS is obtained from IAS by correcting for instrument error, static source error, dynamic pressure error and
options: Magnetic variation
Air density
Aircraft weight
cards.explain: Air density is the fourth correction listed for deriving TAS from IAS.

cards.question: The air density correction applied to airspeed depends on
options: Temperature and aircraft weight
Pressure and temperature
Pressure and humidity
cards.explain: Air density depends on pressure and on temperature.

cards.question: A jet aeroplane climbs from low altitude to high altitude. Which limit governs its maximum speed at the higher altitude?
options: The maximum allowed Mach number MMO
The maximum operating velocity VMO
The never exceed speed VNE
cards.explain: Above a certain altitude the Mach limit MMO takes over from the dynamic pressure limit VMO.

cards.question: Why can the speed limit of a jet aeroplane at low altitude be read directly as an indicated airspeed?
options: Because the limit there depends on dynamic pressure, and the indicated airspeed indicator is a dynamic pressure indicator
Because the limit there depends on dynamic pressure, and the indicated airspeed indicator is a total pressure indicator
Because the limit there depends on the speed of sound, and the indicated airspeed indicator is a dynamic pressure indicator
cards.explain: The indicated airspeed is a dynamic pressure indicator, and at low altitudes the limit depends on the dynamic pressure acting on the aircraft structure, so that limit can be marked as a speed.

cards.question: An aircraft climbs while holding a constant indicated airspeed. What happens to the difference between IAS and TAS?
options: It decreases, because the air density decreases
It stays the same, because the IAS is corrected for density
It increases, because the air density decreases
cards.explain: Falling air density with altitude widens the gap between IAS and TAS.

cards.question: An aircraft is not fitted with an air data computer. What must be provided instead?
options: Correction tables in the aircraft technical log
Correction tables in the Flight Operations Manual
A second airspeed indicator for comparison
cards.explain: Without an air data computer the corrections come from tables in the Flight Operations Manual.

cards.question: What is the purpose of the mach meter
options: To enable flight at the never exceed mach number and with economic efficiency
To enable flight at the maximum operating mach number and with economic efficiency
To enable flight at the maximum operating mach number and with the lowest possible drag
cards.explain: The purpose of the mach meter is to enable flight at the maximum operating mach number, under consideration of economic efficiency.

cards.question: The mach number M is defined as the relation of
options: True airspeed to calibrated airspeed
Speed of sound to speed flown
Speed flown to speed of sound
cards.explain: Mach number is speed flown divided by speed of sound.

cards.question: Which errors is the indicated mach number Mi subject to
options: Static source error and density error
Instrument error and static source error
Instrument error and compressibility error
cards.explain: These are the two errors stated for Mi.

cards.question: In a jet aircraft the speed limit is shown in the airspeed indicator by
options: A red and white VNE pointer
A red and white VMO / MMO pointer
A red and green VMO / MMO pointer
cards.explain: In jet aircraft the limit is shown by the red and white VMO / MMO pointer in the airspeed indicator.

cards.question: On the speed tape of a PFD the speed limit is shown by
options: A red and white area
A red and black area
An amber and black area
cards.explain: The PFD speed tape uses a red and black area.

cards.question: Why is a mach indication needed for flight at high altitude
options: Because the limit there is the maximum operating velocity and dynamic pressure is a function of altitude
Because the limit there is the maximum operating mach number and the speed of sound is a function of dynamic pressure
Because the limit there is the maximum operating mach number and the speed of sound is a function of altitude
cards.explain: At higher altitudes the limit is the maximum operating mach number, and the speed of sound is a function of altitude, so the limit cannot be read from an airspeed alone.

cards.question: What does the shock formation caused by compression of the air do to the airflow and the forces on the aircraft
options: It prevents laminar airflow, increases drag and decreases lift
It prevents laminar airflow, decreases drag and decreases lift
It prevents turbulent airflow, decreases drag and increases lift
cards.explain: Shock formation caused by compression of the air prevents a laminar airflow around the airframe and the airfoils, increases drag and decreases lift.

cards.question: Why can the speed of sound be represented as a function of altitude
options: Because it is a function of temperature, and under standard conditions temperature is a function of altitude
Because it is a function of density, and under standard conditions density is a function of airspeed
Because it is a function of static pressure, and under standard conditions pressure is a function of temperature
cards.explain: The chain given is speed of sound to temperature to altitude.

cards.question: The MMO marking on a stand-alone mach meter is the adjustable version and has to be re-set. Where is this carried out?
options: In the cockpit by the pilot
On the ramp before each flight
In the workshop
cards.explain: Adjusting the MMO marking is a workshop task.

cards.question: From which pressures is the indicated mach number Mi calculated
options: Pitot pressure and accumulator pressure
Pitot pressure and dynamic pressure
Dynamic pressure and cabin pressure
cards.explain: Mi, the indicated mach number, is calculated from pitot pressure and dynamic pressure.

cards.question: The true mach number MT is calculated by
options: The flight management computer
The air data computer
The central maintenance computer
cards.explain: MT, the true mach number, is calculated by the air data computer.

cards.question: Why do jet aircraft need a pointer or speed tape marking to show the maximum allowed airspeed
options: Because the speed limit is a fixed value as the VNE is in piston engine aircraft
Because the airspeed indicator cannot show indicated airspeed above the speed of sound
Because the speed limit is not a fixed value as the VNE is in piston engine aircraft
cards.explain: The limit varies, so it must be displayed, unlike a fixed VNE.

cards.question: An aircraft climbs steadily and the MMO limit falls. Why does it fall?
options: Because the speed of sound decreases
Because the dynamic pressure decreases
Because the compressibility error increases
cards.explain: The falling speed of sound is the stated reason.

cards.question: Why do all jet aircraft have an independent aural overspeed warning
options: Because of the danger of aircraft damage during an overspeed
Because the static source error becomes too large at high altitude
Because the airspeed indicator is unreadable at high mach numbers
cards.explain: The stated reason is the risk of damaging the aircraft.

cards.question: How is the aural overspeed warning produced
options: From the cockpit loudspeakers triggered by the master warning system, or by a separate system with a clacker sound
From the cockpit loudspeakers triggered by the air data computer, or by a separate system with a clacker sound
From the cockpit loudspeakers triggered by the master warning system, or by a separate system with a horn from the stall warning
cards.explain: These are the two arrangements given for the aural warning.

cards.question: A machmeter is opened and found to contain a differential pressure bellows and an aneroid bellows. Which instruments use these same two sensing elements?
options: The altimeter uses a differential pressure capsule and the airspeed indicator an aneroid capsule
The airspeed indicator uses a differential pressure capsule and the vertical speed indicator an aneroid capsule
The airspeed indicator uses a differential pressure capsule and the altimeter an aneroid capsule
cards.explain: The airspeed indicator measures with a differential pressure capsule and the altimeter with an aneroid capsule, and a mach meter contains both of those bellows.

cards.question: A jet aeroplane in high altitude cruise triggers its overspeed warning. Which limit has been exceeded, and does the warning depend on the airspeed indication?
options: MMO, and the detection is taken from the airspeed indication
VMO, and the detection is independent of the airspeed indication
MMO, and the detection is independent of the airspeed indication
cards.explain: At higher altitudes the limit depends on the maximum allowed Mach number, MMO, and the overspeed detection is always independent of the airspeed indication.

cards.question: In which units is the variometer scale calibrated
options: Knots or m/sec
Ft/min or m/sec
Ft/sec or m/min
cards.explain: The scale is calibrated in ft/min or m/sec.

cards.question: What does the abbreviation IVSI stand for
options: Inertial Vertical Speed Indicator
Integrated Vertical Speed Indicator
Instantaneous Vertical Speed Indicator
cards.explain: IVSI is the instantaneous vertical speed indicator, giving undelayed indication.

cards.question: What does the IVSI indicator use to produce its undelayed indication
options: A small fan with a spring loaded vane
A small pump with a spring loaded piston
A small pump with a magnetically held piston
cards.explain: The IVSI indicator uses a small pump with a spring loaded piston.

cards.question: A diaphragm variometer is stripped for overhaul. What seals the air gap?
options: Badger hair
A felt washer
A rubber lip seal
