It is compensated by the pilot each hour
cards.explain: Electrical gyros in commercial aircraft carry automatic drift compensation.

cards.question: Why is the directional gyro more sophisticated than the gyro compass
options: It is part of the instrument panel, not of a remote system
It is part of the remote compass system, not of the panel
It is part of the standby compass, not of the panel
cards.explain: Being a remote system component rather than a panel instrument is the reason given for its greater complexity.

cards.question: The inner frame of a directional gyro leaves the horizontal. What does the liquid level switch signal?
options: The heading synchro
The torque motor
The slaving amplifier
cards.explain: The level switch output goes to the torque motor.

cards.question: To which axis does the levelling torque motor give momentum
options: The axis of the gyro rotor
The axis of the inner frame
The axis of the outer frame
cards.explain: Levelling momentum is applied to the outer frame axis until the inner frame is horizontal.

cards.question: What produces the signals received by the slaving torque motor
options: The earth magnetic field detector
The liquid level switch circuit
The heading synchro amplifier
cards.explain: The slaving signals come from an earth magnetic field detector.

cards.question: A directional gyro is running up after power-on. What rotor speed must be reached before a valid signal is passed?
cards.explain: The monitoring condition for rotor speed is 75%.

cards.question: A pilot is about to adjust the direction indicator after start-up. Which instrument has to be read first?
options: The magnetic compass
The turn indicator
The attitude indicator
cards.explain: The setting value comes from the magnetic compass, which the direction indicator cannot supply itself.

cards.question: A crew finds the gyro compass reading has drifted away from the magnetic compass reading after some minutes of flight. What does that call for?
options: Re-caging the outer frame by hand at regular intervals
Re-levelling the inner frame by hand at regular intervals
Synchronising the course indication by hand at intervals
cards.explain: Because apparent drift, real drift and cardan error spoil the precision, the course indication has to be resynchronised by hand against the magnetic compass.

cards.question: A directional gyro in a remote compass system is found to have no slaving torque motor fitted. What does this mean for its drift?
options: It is removed by the levelling torque motor
It cannot be compensated at all
It is compensated by other means
cards.explain: In remote compass systems the drift can also be compensated by other means than a slaving torque motor.

cards.question: A directional gyro has begun to drift and the slaving momentum is applied to the inner frame axis. Until what point does the slaving continue?
options: Until the inner frame is back in the horizontal
Until the gyro heading matches the flux valve heading
Until the gyro heading matches the standby compass heading
cards.explain: Slaving runs until the gyro agrees with the flux valve, which is the magnetic reference of the system.

cards.question: The servo system of the indicator does not compare correctly. What does the monitoring system of the directional gyro do?
options: It passes no valid signal to the consumer
It passes the flux valve heading instead
It passes a valid signal to the consumer anyway
cards.explain: A correct servo comparison is one of the conditions for a valid signal, so failing it blocks the signal.

cards.question: In which direction do compass systems always point
options: True north
Magnetic north
Compass north
cards.explain: Compass systems follow the earth's magnetic field, which defines magnetic north.

cards.question: What is the angle between true north and magnetic north called
options: Inclination
Deviation
Variation
cards.explain: Variation is the name for the angle between true north and magnetic north.

cards.question: What represents the aircraft longitudinal axis in a heading indication
options: The magnetic needle
The lubber line
The compass scale
cards.explain: The lubber line stands for the longitudinal axis of the aircraft.

cards.question: Which magnetic field lines can a compass use to measure the heading
options: The horizontal ones
The declining ones
The vertical ones
cards.explain: Only the horizontal field lines are usable for heading measurement.

cards.question: Where are all the magnetic field lines horizontal
options: Near the isogonic lines
Near the equator
Near the poles
cards.explain: The field lines run horizontal only in the equatorial region.

cards.question: Which three methods are used to measure the angle between the aircraft longitudinal axis and magnetic north
options: Mechanical, electronic and mathematical
Electronic, mathematical and gyroscopic
Mechanical, electrical and magnetic
cards.explain: The three methods of measuring the angle between the aircraft's longitudinal axis and magnetic north are mechanical, electronic and mathematical.

cards.question: Which electrical part does a direct reading compass contain
options: A torque motor
A light
A detector coil
cards.explain: The only electrical item in a direct reading compass is its light.

cards.question: Where is the standby compass usually located
options: On the centre panel below the front windshields
On the overhead panel above the front windshields
At the centerpost between the front windshields
cards.explain: The usual position is the centerpost between the two front windshields.

cards.question: On which law of magnetism is the function of the magnetic compass based
options: Unlike poles attract and like poles repel
Like poles attract and unlike poles repel
All poles attract when they are close enough
cards.explain: The main law of magnetism quoted is that unlike poles attract and like poles repel.

cards.question: What kind of fluid is used in the compass housing to inhibit the movement of the card
options: A water or glycol based fluid
A silicone or ester based fluid
A mineral or alcohol based fluid
cards.explain: The damping medium named is a mineral or alcohol based fluid.

cards.question: To what does the aircraft magnetic field change the direction of magnetic north
options: Grid north
True north
Compass north
cards.explain: The shifted direction is named compass north.

cards.question: What is the difference between magnetic north and compass north called
options: Inclination
Variation
Deviation
cards.explain: Deviation is the name for that difference.

cards.question: A magnet has magnetic lines running between its poles. What is the effective area of those lines called?
options: The magnetic axis
The magnetic pole
The magnetic field
cards.explain: The area over which the lines act is the magnetic field.

cards.question: How may the earth be regarded in terms of its magnetism
options: As a giant permanent magnet with a bar magnet interior
As a giant electromagnet with a wound coil interior
As a giant permanent magnet with a hollow interior
cards.explain: The earth can be regarded as a giant permanent magnet whose interior is a bar magnet with its ends at the magnetic poles.

cards.question: What does a suspended, free-turning magnetic needle align itself with
options: The earth's magnetic lines
The aircraft's longitudinal axis
The earth's magnetic axis
cards.explain: A free needle takes up the direction of the earth's magnetic lines, which is what makes it usable for navigation.

cards.question: An aircraft is flown to a different part of the world. What does the actual value of the variation depend on?
options: The heading being flown
The aircraft's own magnetic field
The position on earth
cards.explain: Variation is a property of where the aircraft is, not of how it is flown.

cards.question: Between which two directions is the indicated heading measured
options: The aircraft longitudinal axis and the direction to the north pole
The lubber line and the aircraft longitudinal axis
The aircraft lateral axis and the direction to the north pole
cards.explain: Heading is the angle from the aircraft longitudinal axis to north.

cards.question: Why do the different variations at different locations cause no problem in practice
options: Navigation equipment removes the local variation automatically
Navigation equipment, runways and maps all use the magnetic heading
Navigation equipment, runways and maps all use the true heading
cards.explain: Everything is referenced the same way, to magnetic heading, so the local value does not have to be applied.

cards.question: Why must runway headings be updated every few years
options: The position of the magnetic poles is drifting
The position of the geographic poles is drifting
The variation is zero along the isogonic lines
cards.explain: Because the magnetic poles move, anything referenced to them goes out of date.

cards.question: The earth's magnetic field is being resolved at a given latitude. Into which two components is it split?
options: A horizontal and a vertical component
A magnetic and a geographic component
A horizontal and a lateral component
cards.explain: The field is resolved into horizontal and vertical components.

cards.question: An aircraft measures its heading by the electronic method. What determines the angle?
options: A stored variation value
A freely rotating permanent magnet
An earth magnetic field detector
cards.explain: The electronic method senses the field with an earth magnetic field detector.

cards.question: Why is the direct reading compass called the standby compass in commercial aircraft
options: Its indication belongs to the basic T and must always be available
Its indication replaces the gyro indication during every turn
Its indication belongs to the basic T and is the primary one in flight
cards.explain: Being part of the basic T, the heading has to remain available at all times, which is the standby role.

cards.question: Why is the standby compass placed at the centerpost
options: Only one pilot can read it but foreign magnetic fields are distant
Both pilots can read it and foreign magnetic fields are distant
Both pilots can reach it and direct sunlight is avoided
cards.explain: The position suits both crew members and keeps the compass clear of equipment fields.

cards.question: The scale of a standby compass takes up the direction of the field. What turns the scale?
options: A permanent magnet
A torque motor
An electromagnet
cards.explain: The scale is driven by a permanent magnet aligning with the field.

cards.question: Why is the direct reading compass filled with a fluid
options: To lubricate the compass scale bearings
To insulate the compass scale from heat
To dampen the compass scale movements
cards.explain: The fluid is there as a damping medium for the scale.

cards.question: With what does the freely moving magnet of a compass line up
options: The longitudinal axis of the aircraft
The vertical components of the earth's field
The horizontal components of the earth's field
cards.explain: The compass magnet follows the horizontal components of the earth's field.

cards.question: What does the compass card under the lubber line show
options: The magnetic field against the aircraft's longitudinal axis
The longitudinal axis against the earth's magnetic pole
The longitudinal axis against the earth's geographic pole
cards.explain: The reading at the lubber line is the longitudinal axis direction against the earth's magnetic pole.

cards.question: What condition must be met for the lubber line to represent the aircraft longitudinal axis
options: The compass must be correctly compensated
The compass must be correctly filled
The compass must be correctly installed
cards.explain: The lubber line only stands for the longitudinal axis if the installation is correct.

cards.question: The earth's magnetic field is weak. What does this mean for the compass magnet?
options: A high inclination of the compass magnet
A high directive force of the compass magnet
A low directive force of the compass magnet
cards.explain: A weak field gives the compass magnet only a weak directive force.

cards.question: The damping medium changes volume with temperature. What balances this out?
options: Washers
Slots
Bellows
cards.explain: Bellows take up the expansion and contraction of the damping fluid.

cards.question: What inside the aircraft also affects the direct reading compass
options: A magnetic field from electrical equipment
A vibration field from electrical equipment
A magnetic field from the earth's interior
cards.explain: Equipment running in normal operation sets up a magnetic field inside the aircraft.

cards.question: A standby compass is found to have a compass error from the airframe. What is used to minimize it?
options: Small adjustable magnets inside the compass
Copper washers under the mounting plate
Small adjustable weights inside the compass
cards.explain: The compass compensation consists of small adjustable magnets inside the instrument.

cards.question: Why does the north pole of the magnetic needle show north
options: The magnetic south pole of the earth is there
The magnetic north pole of the earth is there
The geographic south pole of the earth is there
cards.explain: What lies at the earth's north is a magnetic south pole, and unlike poles attract.

cards.question: An aircraft carries a modern inertial reference unit. Why is a compass reference carried as well?
options: Radio indications are referenced to magnetic north
Inertial units cannot produce a heading at all
Inertial units are accurate for a short time only
cards.explain: Even with INS or IRS fitted, indications such as the VOR RMI are referenced to magnetic north.

cards.question: An aircraft is to operate in a region close to the magnetic pole. Which heading source must be used there and why?
options: A flux valve, because the vertical component takes over
A directional gyro, because the horizontal component is too weak
A standby compass, because the horizontal component is strongest
cards.explain: Inclination leaves too little horizontal field at high latitude, so a gyro or inertial reference replaces the compass.

cards.question: A compass finds the angle with a mounted, freely rotating permanent magnet. Which method is this and which kind of compass?
options: The electronic method, a remote reading compass
The mechanical method, a remote reading compass
The mechanical method, a direct reading compass
cards.explain: The magnetic needle principle is the mechanical method and gives the direct reading compass.

cards.question: An aircraft finds its heading from data held in a computer rather than by sensing the field. Which method is this and what does it use?
options: The mathematical method, using the stored variation for each location
The electronic method, using the field detector fitted at each location
The mechanical method, using the magnet mounted at each location
cards.explain: Working from stored variation values in a navigation computer is the mathematical method.

cards.question: Fluid damping has been accepted so the indicator stays stable under vibration. What has to be accepted along with it?
options: A loss of directive force of the magnet
A time delay after a change of direction
An increase of the installation error
cards.explain: The time delay following a change of direction is an unavoidable disadvantage of keeping the indicator stable against vibration.

cards.question: A compass is about to be compensated. Into which classes are its errors divided?
options: A, B and D errors
B, C and D errors
A, B and C errors
cards.explain: The errors to be eliminated by compensation are classed as A, B and C errors.

cards.question: A compass is found to carry a B error — in which directions does it show up?
options: in all directions
in the east-west direction
in the north-south direction
cards.explain: A B error is the east-west error.

cards.question: An engineer is picking out tools for a compass compensation — which ones may be used?
options: only approved antimagnetic tools
only calibrated torque tools
only insulated electrical tools
cards.explain: Compensation may only be done with approved antimagnetic tools.

cards.question: Within what tolerance must the aircraft be aligned to North - South before the SCC is used
options: +/− 2 degrees
+/− 10 degrees
+/− 5 degrees
cards.explain: The alignment requirement is exactly +/- 2 degrees of North - South.

cards.question: What is required of the deviation that is left once a compensation has been performed
options: it should be as small as possible
it should be below one degree on every heading
it should be exactly zero on every heading
cards.explain: The requirement is that the deviation is as small as possible.

cards.question: In what steps are the headings checked when a deviation card is made up
options: in steps of 10 degrees
in steps of 45 degrees
in steps of 30 degrees
cards.explain: Headings are checked every 30 degrees.

cards.question: An aircraft is flying over the northern part of the earth — in which direction does the vertical component of the field point there?
options: downwards
along the meridian
upwards
cards.explain: Over the northern part the vertical component points down.

cards.question: In which direction of flight does an acceleration or a deceleration leave the heading indication unchanged
options: a northerly direction
a westerly direction
an easterly direction
cards.explain: On a northerly heading an acceleration or deceleration leaves the indication alone.

cards.question: Why does a magnetic compass or a remote compass system have to be compensated at all
options: the earth's field loses strength as the aircraft climbs away from the ground
the vertical field component pulls the magnet out of the horizontal plane
aircraft ferro- and electro-magnetism sets up fields that cause a deviation
cards.explain: Interference fields from the aircraft's own ferro- and electro-magnetism produce the deviation.

cards.question: Some error is still left after a compass has been compensated — where is that remainder written down?
options: on the compensating disc at the airport site
on a deviation card carried on the aircraft
on a label fitted beside the flux valve
cards.explain: The remaining deviation goes on the deviation card that stays on the aircraft.

cards.question: An indication is falsified by the amount of the deviation — what is that heading called?
options: the compass heading
the true heading
the magnetic heading
cards.explain: The falsified indication is named the compass heading.

cards.question: An engineer walks out to compensate a compass. Which of the items he is carrying can deflect the compass?
options: his ear defenders, his gloves and his torch
his glasses, his watch and his mobile phone
his notebook, his pen and his pass
cards.explain: Glasses, a watch and a mobile phone are the items named as causing deflection.

cards.question: What can be done with the Standby Compass Calibrator without physically turning the aircraft
options: measure the vertical component of the earth's field at the compass
compensate permanent magnetisation errors and complete the deviation card
set the directional gyro to agree with the remote compass heading
cards.explain: The SCC compensates permanent magnetisation errors and completes the deviation card with the aircraft standing still.

cards.question: Which two separate functions does the SCC perform
options: it cancels the aircraft's permanent field and adds a vertical field
it rotates the standby compass and records the resulting deviation
it cancels the local earth's field and adds a rotatable standard field
cards.explain: The SCC cancels the local earth's field and adds a standard field that can be rotated.

cards.question: The aircraft cannot be put exactly on North - South for a standby compass calibration — what is done about the residual misalignment?
options: it is entered on the deviation card
it is taken out on the E−W screw
it is measured and set into the SCC
cards.explain: The misalignment is measured and fed into the SCC itself.

cards.question: A compensation is finished and a small deviation is still there — why can it not be driven to zero?
options: the compensation is only checked on two headings
the means of adjustment cannot do any better
the earth's field changes while the aircraft is turned
cards.explain: Zero cannot practically be reached with the available means of adjustment.

cards.question: The readings have been taken on every checked heading — what is done with each of them?
options: each one is recorded in the compensation log
each one is recorded on a deviation card
each one is set into the remote compensator
cards.explain: Each checked heading's reading goes onto the deviation card.

cards.question: A compass magnet is kept level on its bearing — which component of the earth's field does it then measure?
options: the horizontal component
the vertical component
the total resultant field
cards.explain: Holding the magnet horizontal lets it measure the horizontal component.

cards.question: What decides whether a tilted compass turns to the right or to the left
options: the actual heading of the aircraft
the actual bank angle of the aircraft
the actual airspeed of the aircraft
cards.explain: The direction of the swing depends on the heading the aircraft is on.

cards.question: A compass has been tilted out of the horizontal plane during an acceleration — what does the crew see?
options: a slowly spinning card
a frozen heading
a falsified heading
cards.explain: The result at the instrument is a falsified heading.

cards.question: Why is there no heading error when the aircraft accelerates on a northerly heading
options: the magnet is held exactly horizontal by its bearing on that heading
the vertical field acts on the magnet the way the horizontal field does
the vertical field has no component at all at that position on the earth
cards.explain: Both field components pull the magnet the same way, so nothing moves.

cards.question: Why does a southerly heading behave like a northerly one during an acceleration
options: the permanent magnet points in the same direction
the pivot point bearing locks the compass scale
the vertical component reverses with the hemisphere
cards.explain: On south the permanent magnet still points the same way, so the same reasoning holds.

cards.question: Compensation is being worked from INS/IRS data alongside the aircraft's own heading sources — which source supplies the magnetic heading?
options: the INS/IRS
the standby compass
the remote compass system
cards.explain: The remote compass gives magnetic heading, the INS/IRS gives true heading.

cards.question: A remote compass is 4 ° off the target course on one of the four main headings. What does that mean for the compensation?
options: it is out of tolerance and must be adjusted further
it is in tolerance and the 30° headings can be started
it is in tolerance for a main heading but not for a 30° heading
cards.explain: The remote compass tolerance is + / − 2 °, so 4 ° is outside it and more adjustment is needed.

cards.question: An acceleration has tilted a compass out of the horizontal plane — what now acts on its magnet?
options: the permanent magnetism of the aircraft structure
the vertical component of the earth's magnetic field
the horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field
cards.explain: Once the compass is off the horizontal the vertical component starts to influence the magnet.

cards.question: A remote compass system is fitted to an aircraft. Which two sensing devices does it use?
options: a sensor for the earth's magnetic field and a vertical gyro
a sensor for the aircraft's own field and a rate gyro
a sensor for the earth's magnetic field and a directional gyro
cards.explain: The system pairs an earth's field sensor with a directional gyro.

cards.question: Where is the indicator of a remote compass system fitted
options: in a wing tip fairing
in the avionics compartment
in the instrument panel
cards.explain: The indicator sits in the instrument panel.

cards.question: What does the flux valve turn the direction of the magnetic field into
options: a proportional mechanical rotation
a proportional electrical signal
a proportional change of resistance
cards.explain: The output is an electrical signal proportional to the field direction.

cards.question: A large aeroplane carries two separate remote compass systems — how are they shared out?
options: one for each engine
one for each pilot
one for each gyro platform
cards.explain: The two systems are split one per pilot.

cards.question: What does the signal detected by the flux valve represent
options: the strength of the earth's vertical field at the aircraft's longitudinal axis
the direction of the earth's horizontal field to the aircraft's longitudinal axis
the angle between the directional gyro and the aircraft's longitudinal axis
cards.explain: The flux valve signal gives the direction of the earth's horizontal field relative to the aircraft's longitudinal axis.

cards.question: A flux valve has to stay level as the aircraft manoeuvres — how is it suspended in its housing?
options: on a full cardanic suspension
on a needle point bearing
on three rubber mounts
cards.explain: It hangs in a full cardan suspension.

cards.question: On what do the intensity and the direction of the sensing coil signals depend
options: on where the magnetic field points
on how fast the aircraft is turning
on how strong the excitation current is
cards.explain: Both the intensity and the direction follow the direction of the magnetic field.

cards.question: Under which condition does a coil induce a voltage at all
options: only when the iron core has reached full saturation
only when the intensity of the magnetic field is highest
only when the intensity of the magnetic field changes
cards.explain: A changing field intensity is what induces the voltage.

cards.question: How is the iron core of the flux valve made to change its magnetic state
options: it is frequently demagnetised by a direct current in a sensing coil
it is frequently turned by a small motor inside the housing
it is frequently saturated by an alternating current in an excitation coil
cards.explain: An alternating current in the excitation coil repeatedly saturates the core.

cards.question: What gives the flux valve its name
options: the alternate switching of the magnetic field
the liquid that flows through its hemisphere
the vent valve that breathes with altitude
cards.explain: The field is switched on and off like a valve, which is where the name comes from.

cards.question: An aircraft is held in a 40° banked turn — what happens to the flux valve measuring plane?
options: it stays horizontal because the cardan takes any angle
it is driven back to horizontal by the directional gyro
it can no longer stay horizontal
cards.explain: The cardan only holds the plane level out to about 30°, so at 40° of bank it is exceeded.

cards.question: The excitation current has just fallen away and the core has come out of saturation — what does the magnetic field do?
options: it takes the shortest way and bypasses the three coils
it takes an even longer way through the iron and the coils
it collapses completely until the core saturates again
cards.explain: Unsaturated iron offers a far easier path, so the field runs the longer way through the iron and the coils.

cards.question: A flux valve output and an ordinary synchro output are compared on an oscilloscope. How does the sinusoidal voltage pattern of the flux valve differ?
options: it is shifted near to the peak value of the excitation voltage
it is clipped at the saturation level of the iron core
it is shifted near to the zero value of the excitation voltage
cards.explain: In the flux valve the pattern sits near the zero value of the excitation voltage.

cards.question: A compass coupler is getting no setting signal at all — which chain has broken down?
options: the directional gyro to flux valve drive path
the compass coupler to excitation coil feed path
the flux valve to control transformer path
cards.explain: The path runs flux valve to control transformer to the directional gyro or compass coupler, so a loss at the coupler points back along that path.

questions.question: Where on an aeroplane are the flux valves located
options: at the wing tips, in the vertical stabiliser or in the tail cone
in the nose radome, in the forward cargo bay or in the wheel well
under the cockpit floor, in the engine pylons or in the centre tank
questions.explain: Those three positions are the ones used for the flux valve on an aeroplane.

questions.question: A directional gyro is left running for a long flight leg. Which disadvantage shows up?
options: a falsified heading during accelerations and turns
a falsified reading in the region of the magnetic poles
a drift of the indication as the time passes
questions.explain: Drift is the disadvantage of the gyro based direction instruments.

questions.question: Where are the amplifiers that raise the voltage of weak signals installed
options: in the integrated instrument system rack
in the automatic direction finder indicator
in the housing of the directional gyro
questions.explain: Weak signals such as the compass rose motor voltage are amplified in the IIS rack.

questions.question: How is the A error of a remote compass system compensated
options: by turning the compensation device screws
by turning the whole flux valve
by turning the remote compensator potentiometer
questions.explain: The A error is taken out by rotating the valve itself, not by a screw or a potentiometer.

questions.question: To which value does fast synchronisation raise the update rate of the magnetic heading
options: 7 °/min.
questions.explain: Fast synchronisation runs at seven hundred degrees a minute.

questions.question: A helicopter flux valve is to be relocated and the shop asks what rules the choice of place. What governs it?
options: it must be inside the cabin of the helicopter to keep the run short
it must be far away from all magnetic fields of the helicopter
it must be close to the gearbox of the helicopter for a rigid mount
questions.explain: Distance from the helicopter's own magnetic fields decides where the flux valve goes.

questions.question: What shows the pilot that the signal from his compass system is not valid
options: a heading warning flag
the compass superflag
the synchronising annunciator
questions.explain: Loss of validity is shown by the heading warning flag.

questions.question: To which autoflight system is the heading of compass system 1 provided
options: to autoflight system number 2
to both autoflight systems together
to autoflight system number 1
questions.explain: The autoflight systems are fed straight across, one for one.

questions.question: Why does a large aircraft carry a third display computer
options: To drive the control panels
To convert analogue inputs
For redundancy
questions.explain: The third computer is fitted on large aircraft for redundancy.

questions.question: Which of the two EICAS displays on a Boeing aircraft carries the engine and warning indications
options: The lower EICAS display
The auxiliary EICAS display
The upper EICAS display
questions.explain: The upper EICAS is the engine and warning display and the auxiliary one is the system display.

questions.question: Which kind of information does the primary flight display supply
options: Flight planning information and parameters
Flight monitoring information and parameters
Engine monitoring information and parameters
questions.explain: The primary flight display is the flight monitoring display.

questions.question: Which three items are controlled by the avionics warning electronics assembly itself?
options: The master warning light, the aural warn speaker and the stick shaker
The master caution light, the aural warn speaker and the stick shaker
The master warning light, the aural warn speaker and the display units
questions.explain: Those three are the items it drives directly.

questions.question: What becomes of the information that is normally presented in the colour of a failed electron beam
options: It will not be shown
It is shown as a flag instead
It is shown in white instead
questions.explain: Information carried by the missing colour simply disappears from the screen.

questions.question: Which part of the display is affected when one input signal to a display unit is lost
options: Only the warning labels of the display
Only the indication of the related parameter
The whole of the display unit
questions.explain: Only the indication belonging to the missing signal goes away.

questions.question: Under which condition is the head up display meant to give guidance information on the ground and at take-off and landing
options: When visibility is reduced
When the landing gear is extended
When the autopilot is engaged
questions.explain: That guidance is provided for the case of reduced visibility.

questions.question: Which automatic procedure is the head up display used to monitor?
options: The auto thrust reduction
The auto land flare
The auto approach
questions.explain: One stated purpose is to monitor the auto approach.

questions.question: Which navigation point does the basic waypoint data on the ND refer to
options: The last one passed
The next one
The destination one
questions.explain: The waypoint data gives information about the next navigation point.

questions.question: Which ND parameter comes from somewhere other than the navigation systems
options: The wind velocity
The heading
The ground speed
questions.explain: Apart from the heading, all information on the ND is based on data from the navigation systems.

questions.question: What does the information on a central warning display describe
options: The present failure condition
The maintenance action already carried out
The flight phase being computed
questions.explain: The displays describe the present failure condition.

questions.question: One of the two ECAM displays has failed, so which symbol appears in the lower part of the engine/warning display?
options: RCL
STS
ADV
questions.explain: With only one ECAM display left, ECAM works as a mono display and ADV is shown.

questions.question: A pushbutton carries an amber FAULT legend, so how urgent is the crew action?
options: Action is needed at once
Action is not needed at all
Action is needed but not at once
questions.explain: Amber is used when action is required but not necessarily at once.

questions.question: A fault occurs in a system whose local light is on the overhead panel out of the pilot's sight, so how does the crew learn which system it is?
options: The master caution light names the affected system
The centralised caution panel names the affected system
The overhead local light is repeated on the glareshield
questions.explain: The master light says only that something is wrong, so the panel at eye level is what identifies the system.

questions.question: A pilot sees STS in the lower part of the engine/warning display but no status page is being shown, so where will that status page appear once it is called up?
options: On the system display
On the centralised caution panel
On the engine/warning display
questions.explain: STS says a status page is available and the status page is displayed on the SD.

questions.question: The status pushbutton has been pressed and after a short time the normal display returns on its own, so what does that tell the crew?
options: No status messages are present
The status page has been cleared by CLR
The ECAM is working as a mono display
questions.explain: The normal messages come back by themselves only when there are no status messages to show.

questions.question: A pilot wants to see a second system page while one is already up, so what happens to the page already displayed?
options: It stays, because two pages can be shown side by side
It stays, because the second page opens on the E/WD
It is replaced, because only one can be shown at a time
questions.explain: Only one of the twelve system pages can be displayed at any one time.

questions.question: An engine fire breaks out in flight, so what must the crew do about it?
options: Note it and continue, as the flight is not affected
React immediately, as it is a real emergency
React before the next flight phase begins
questions.explain: Engine fire is a level 3 warning and a level 3 warning is a real emergency needing an immediate reaction.

questions.question: A single chime sounds and the master caution light comes on, so what does the crew know about the failure?
options: It has no direct influence on the flight
It is a real emergency needing an immediate reaction
It gives no aural alarm and no warning light
questions.explain: A single chime with the master caution light is a level 2, and level 2 failures have no direct influence on the flight.

questions.question: A recorder fault and a stall warning occur in the same flight, so how do the two alerts differ in what the crew gets?
options: Each one gives an aural alarm but only one gives a light
One gives no sound or light while the other gives both
One gives a single chime while the other gives no sound
questions.explain: A recorder fault is a level 1 with no aural alarm or warning light, while a stall warning is a level 3 with an aural alarm and a flashing master warning light.

questions.question: An aircraft has just been powered up and no selection has been made, so what is seen on the two EICAS display units?
options: Primary engine data above and the status information below
Primary engine data above and secondary engine data below
Secondary engine data above and primary engine data below
questions.explain: After power-up the upper unit shows the primary and the lower unit the secondary engine data.

questions.question: Every indication that is not needed has been removed from the main EICAS display, so which two groups are still shown?
options: The cabin altitude and the duct pressure readouts
The landing gear status and the flap indications
The primary engine parameters and the fuel system data
questions.explain: Those two groups are the ones stated to show at all times.

questions.question: An engine exceedance occurs while the aeroplane stands with its parking brake set, so what becomes of the event?
options: It is lost, since two engines have to be running
It is stored, since that storage is not inhibited
It is lost, since the brake has to be released first
questions.explain: Engine exceedance page storage is not inhibited, so the running and brake conditions do not apply to it.

questions.question: Rising ground is approached at 2600 ft radio altitude, so why does the basic GPWS stay quiet?
options: Its aural alerts are suppressed with the landing gear up
Its boundaries are computed from the barometric altitude
Its automatic operation begins at a lower height
questions.explain: The aircraft is still above the radio altitude at which the basic system begins to operate automatically.

questions.question: The limits of one of the alerting envelopes are exceeded, so what does the enhanced system give the flight crew?
options: Aural alert messages with visual annunciations and displays
A master warning that has to be reset by the crew
An automatic pull-up commanded through the autopilot
questions.explain: Exceeding an envelope limit produces aural messages together with visual annunciations and displays.

questions.question: A system is required to see steep rising ground that the downward looking sensor would find too late, so which protection is needed?
options: The terrain clearance floor protection
The modulation of the alerting envelopes
The terrain data base look ahead protection
questions.explain: Look ahead protection works from the database instead of the downward looking sensor.

questions.question: The terrain awareness display function has been lost, so what happens to the ground proximity warning functions?
options: They are lost together with the display function
They go on working while the necessary inputs are there
They fall back to the excessive descent rate mode
questions.explain: The warning functions keep working as long as their inputs remain available.

questions.question: The crew reduces the descent rate as soon as the first mode 1 message is heard, so which boundary has not been penetrated?
options: The inner alert boundary
The outer alert boundary
The upper alert boundary
questions.explain: The first message comes from the outer boundary, so the inner one has still not been crossed.

questions.question: The flaps are at the landing position and the aircraft is within two dots of the localizer on an ILS approach, so which submode boundary applies?
options: Mode 2A
Mode 4B
Mode 2B
questions.explain: That configuration is one of those listed for mode 2B.

questions.question: Which mode uses altitude above sea level information in its computation
options: Mode 3
Mode 2
Mode 1
questions.explain: Mode 3 is the mode whose computation is stated to take altitude above sea level information, while mode 1 works from vertical speed and radio altitude and mode 2 from vertical speed and radio altitude.

questions.question: An approach is flown at 140 knots with the gear down and the flaps still up, so which submode watches the terrain clearance?
options: Mode 4B
Mode 4A
Mode 4C
questions.explain: Mode 4B is the submode that applies once the landing gear is lowered.

questions.question: The aircraft drifts 1.5 dots below the beam centre at 800 feet radio altitude, so which activation occurs?
options: No alert activation at all
The soft alert activation
The hard alert activation
questions.explain: The aircraft is beyond 1.3 dots below the beam centre, so the soft alert comes; the hard alert needs below 300 feet radio altitude and more than 2 dots.

cards.question: Where on an aeroplane are the flux valves located
options: in the nose radome, in the forward cargo bay or in the wheel well
at the wing tips, in the vertical stabiliser or in the tail cone
under the cockpit floor, in the engine pylons or in the centre tank
cards.explain: Those three positions are the ones used for the flux valve on an aeroplane.

cards.question: Where is the flux valve of a helicopter usually installed
options: under the cockpit floor, in the nose compartment or on the landing gear skid
on the roof of the cabin, in the rotor head or on the upper deck of the engine
on the bottom of the tail boom, the vertical stabilizers or in the vertical fin
cards.explain: Those are the usual installation places for the flux valve of a helicopter.

cards.question: A directional gyro is left running for a long flight leg. Which disadvantage shows up?
options: a falsified reading in the region of the magnetic poles
a falsified heading during accelerations and turns
a drift of the indication as the time passes
cards.explain: Drift is the disadvantage of the gyro based direction instruments.

cards.question: Which disadvantage do magnet compasses and flux valves have
options: a drift which grows with the running time of the unit
a heading which lags behind by a fixed amount in the climb
a falsified heading during accelerations and turns
cards.explain: Accelerations and turns are what falsify the magnetic sensing devices.

cards.question: What do the two acronyms in the name ADF RMI stand for
options: Automatic Direction Finder and Radio Magnetic Indicator
Airborne Direction Finder and Radio Magnetic Instrument
Automatic Deviation Finder and Remote Magnetic Indicator
cards.explain: ADF is Automatic Direction Finder and RMI is Radio Magnetic Indicator.

cards.question: What do the arrows in the ADF RMI point to
options: the stations that are tuned in
the magnetic north found by the flux valve
the course selected on the compass rose
cards.explain: The ADF arrows point at whichever broadcast stations have been tuned.

cards.question: Which three units does a remote compass with ADF/RMI have
options: a flux valve, a directional gyro and an ADF/RMI
a directional gyro, a compass coupler and a compass controller
a flux valve, a compass coupler and an ADF/RMI
cards.explain: Those three are the units listed for the remote compass with ADF/RMI.

cards.question: Where are the amplifiers that raise the voltage of weak signals installed
options: in the integrated instrument system rack
in the automatic direction finder indicator
in the housing of the directional gyro
cards.explain: Weak signals such as the compass rose motor voltage are amplified in the IIS rack.

cards.question: Which errors are adjusted by the screws on the flux valve compensation device
options: the A and B errors
the A error only
the B and C errors
cards.explain: The screws on the compensation device take out the B and C errors.

cards.question: How is the A error of a remote compass system compensated
options: by turning the remote compensator potentiometer
by turning the whole flux valve
by turning the compensation device screws
cards.explain: The A error is taken out by rotating the valve itself, not by a screw or a potentiometer.

cards.question: Which units make up a remote compass system with a compass coupler
options: flux valve, DG, ADF RMI and compass coupler
flux valve, DG, compass controller and remote compensator
flux valve, DG, compass controller and compass coupler
cards.explain: Those four are the units listed for the coupler based system.

cards.question: With which control can any desired heading be set
options: the DG − SLAVED switch
the SET HDG knob
the synchronizing knob
cards.explain: The SET HDG knob is the one for setting a heading of choice.

cards.question: Fast synchronisation is unserviceable on a compass system. Where is the control logic for it held?
options: in the compass controller
in the directional gyro
in the compass coupler
cards.explain: The fast synchronisation logic sits inside the coupler.

cards.question: To which value does fast synchronisation raise the update rate of the magnetic heading
options: 7 °/min.
cards.explain: Fast synchronisation runs at seven hundred degrees a minute.

cards.question: A flux valve is to go at a wing tip rather than near the cabin. Why is that place chosen?
options: to keep them inside the pressurised area so they can be reached in flight
to exclude the influence of magnetic interference fields as far as possible
to bring them as close as possible to the heading indicators they supply
cards.explain: The locations are chosen to keep magnetic interference fields away from the valve.

cards.question: A helicopter flux valve is to be relocated and the shop asks what rules the choice of place. What governs it?
options: it must be inside the cabin of the helicopter to keep the run short
it must be close to the gearbox of the helicopter for a rigid mount
it must be far away from all magnetic fields of the helicopter
cards.explain: Distance from the helicopter's own magnetic fields decides where the flux valve goes.

cards.question: Why is the heading of a flux valve falsified while the aircraft accelerates
options: the valve loses part of its excitation while the aircraft is accelerating
the valve swings so that it is also affected by the vertical magnetic field
the valve output is damped so that it follows the change far too slowly
cards.explain: The swing lets the vertical component of the earth's field reach the valve.

cards.question: Which two units are combined to build a remote compass system that shows the correct heading
options: a flux valve and a magnet compass
a directional gyro and a magnet compass
a flux valve and a directional gyro
cards.explain: The flux valve and the directional gyro together make the remote compass system.

cards.question: From which unit does the indicator of a remote compass system receive the stable heading information
options: from the directional gyro
from the flux valve
from the magnet compass
cards.explain: Stable heading comes to the indicator from the directional gyro.

cards.question: How is the difference between the magnetic field direction and the indicated heading used
options: it drives the compass rose of the indicator directly
it changes the excitation voltage of the flux valve
it adjusts the DG through a torque motor
cards.explain: The difference signal is fed to a torque motor which moves the gyro.

cards.question: The slaving torque motor applies a torque to the gyro. What does that torque produce?
options: a precession which changes the DG direction
a friction brake which holds the DG direction
a rigidity which locks the DG to magnetic north
cards.explain: Torque on a gyro acts as precession and so moves the gyro's direction.

cards.question: A crew has one ADF RMI on the panel. Which two kinds of information does it give them?
options: a radio navigation indication and the aircraft attitude
the magnetic heading and the distance to the station
a radio navigation indication and the magnetic heading
cards.explain: The one indicator carries both the radio navigation picture and the magnetic heading.

cards.question: What does the slaving annunciator show the pilot
options: the difference between the indicated heading and the flux valve signal
the difference between the excitation voltage and its nominal value
the difference between the selected course and the indicated heading
cards.explain: The annunciator displays how far the indicated heading is from what the flux valve says.

cards.question: In the ADF/RMI system, where is the difference between the indicated heading and the flux valve signal detected
options: inside the compass coupler
inside the flux valve
inside the indicator itself
cards.explain: In this architecture the detection happens in the indicator itself.

cards.question: A pilot reaches for the synchronizing knob on the ADF RMI. What can he change with it?
options: the rate at which the torque motor runs
the mode in which the system operates
the indication of the compass rose
cards.explain: The knob acts on what the compass rose shows.

cards.question: What is protected by the fuse fitted in the integrated instrument system rack
options: the torque motor which is fitted inside the directional gyro
the transformer which supplies the flux valve excitation
the amplifier which raises the compass rose motor voltage
cards.explain: That fuse is there for the excitation transformer of the flux valve.

cards.question: In which form does the detected field direction reach the control transformer in the indicator
options: as a direct current signal
as a single-phase signal
as a three-phase signal
cards.explain: The flux valve passes its direction information on as a three-phase signal.

cards.question: A slaving control transformer is fitted in an ADF/RMI. What is its rotor connected to?
options: the compass card
the synchronisation knob
the slaving torque motor
cards.explain: The rotor of the slaving CT is driven directly by the compass card.

cards.question: The north found by the flux valve matches the position of the compass rose. What appears at the slaving CT output?
options: a steady direct voltage
a signal of maximum size
no signal at all
cards.explain: Agreement between the two gives a null at the control transformer.

cards.question: In which condition of flight does the information from the flux valve contain no errors?
options: when flying at a constant height in any manoeuvre
when flying straight ahead without acceleration
when flying a steady turn at a constant bank angle
cards.explain: Unaccelerated straight flight is the condition in which the valve is error free.

cards.question: Which precision of heading indication is possible all the time with the remote compass system
cards.explain: Two degrees either way is the precision of the remote compass system.

cards.question: Where is the amplified error signal from the control transformer sent
options: to the slaving torque motor
to the compass rose motor
to the flux valve signal coils
cards.explain: The amplified error signal drives the slaving torque motor on the gyro.

cards.question: After switch on the gyro is not aligned with magnetic north. How long can the automatic alignment take?
options: up to 90 minutes
up to 9 minutes
up to 90 seconds
cards.explain: Working off a large error at the slow torquing rate can take as long as ninety minutes.

cards.question: The annunciator needle of the ADF/RMI sits at its central position. What does this mean?
options: the system is in the free azimuth mode
the slaving amplifier has failed
the slaving CD is zeroed out
cards.explain: Centre position of the moving coil annunciator means the slaving CD is nulled.

cards.question: What does the annunciator on the ADF/RMI display
options: the output voltage of the slaving amplifier
the output voltage of the slaving torque motor
the excitation voltage supplied to the flux valve
cards.explain: The moving coil annunciator reads the slaving amplifier output.

cards.question: Between which two units can a remote compensator be switched
options: flux valve and directional gyro
flux valve and compass coupler
compass coupler and compass controller
cards.explain: The remote compensator sits in the line between the flux valve and the coupler.

cards.question: A meter is put on the supply output of a remote compensator. Which kind of voltage is there?
options: a variable low frequency AC voltage
an extremely constant DC voltage
an extremely constant three-phase voltage
cards.explain: The compensating supply is a very constant direct voltage.

cards.question: How is the compensation device carrying the B and C error adjustment screws fitted
options: it is screwed into the compass coupler
it is wired in series with the excitation coil
it is screwed onto the flux valve
cards.explain: The compensation device is mounted directly on the flux valve.

cards.question: A compensation device is to be fitted to a flux valve. In which case is this done?
options: only in the case of a failed remote compensator
only in the case of persistent interference fields
only in the case of a drifting directional gyro
cards.explain: It is reserved for interference fields that will not go away.

cards.question: A newer type of compass system is fitted. Where is the fuse for the flux valve excitation transformer additionally installed?
options: in the flux valve housing
in the compass coupler
in the compass controller
cards.explain: On newer couplers the protecting fuse is also carried in the coupler.

cards.question: The synchronising annunciator is deflected. Along which path is the difference being reported?
options: flux valve − coupler − DG
DG − coupler − autoflight system
flux valve − coupler − HSI
cards.explain: It watches the chain from the valve through the coupler to the gyro heading.

cards.question: Which two signals are coupled together in the compass coupler in the slaved mode
options: the DG platform heading and the autoflight heading
the flux valve signal and the DG platform heading
the flux valve signal and the selected VOR course
cards.explain: Slaved mode brings the valve signal and the gyro heading together in the coupler.

cards.question: Flux valve and gyro headings disagree in a coupler system. Which device balances them out?
options: a control transformer
a differential synchro
a slaving torque motor
cards.explain: The differential synchro in the coupler takes out the difference.

cards.question: A compass coupler system is compared with a system using an ADF/RMI. What does the comparison show?
options: the same indication behaviour and the same precision
a worse indication behaviour but a higher precision
a better indication behaviour but a lower precision
cards.explain: There is no difference between the two systems in indication behaviour or in precision.

cards.question: The system is in its run-up phase. What happens to the update rate of the differential synchro?
options: it is held at 2°/min.
it is increased to 700°/min.
it is reduced to 0.2°/min.
cards.explain: Run-up uses the much higher rate so the system lines up quickly.

cards.question: Which source provides the directional information in the DG mode
options: only the short-term stable gyro platform
only the long-term stable flux valve
the gyro platform and the flux valve together
cards.explain: In DG mode the gyro alone supplies the direction.

cards.question: What is the state of the synchronising annunciator in the DG mode
options: it stands at its centre
it shows the drift rate
it is switched off
cards.explain: There is nothing for it to compare in DG mode, so it is switched off.

cards.question: How does the fast synchronisation control logic raise the update rate
options: by bypassing the differential synchro
by switching in a second torque motor
by switching the amplification factor
cards.explain: A change of amplification factor is what gives the higher rate.

cards.question: After which length of switch-off pause does switching on in SLAVED mode start the fast synchronisation
options: about 10 seconds
about 2 seconds
about 2 minutes
cards.explain: A pause of roughly two minutes before a SLAVED start triggers the logic.

cards.question: What is gained by holding the torquing rate of the directional gyro to its printed maximum
options: drift is still compensated but accelerations cannot move the indication
alignment is faster but the gyro cannot be moved by its own drift
turns are still compensated but drift cannot move the indication
cards.explain: The rate is fast enough for drift but too slow for the short acceleration errors to get through.

cards.question: An aircraft is in a long accelerating climb and the flux valve signal is briefly false. Why does the indicated heading stay good?
options: the torque motor reverses and drives the gyro back to its old heading
the gyro can be torqued only slowly, so a brief error cannot move it
the flux valve signal is cut off automatically whenever speed changes
cards.explain: The slow torquing rate means a short lived false signal has no time to shift the indication.

cards.question: In the cruise the slaving annunciator keeps fluctuating around zero. What does this tell the pilot?
options: the gyro is still running up and the heading is not yet usable at all
the gyro has lost its stable direction and the valve is being ignored
the gyro has the correct stable direction and the valve is correcting it
cards.explain: Fluctuation about zero is the sign of a healthy system doing its normal correcting.

cards.question: The slaving annunciator shows a long term deflection to one side. What should be concluded?
options: the flux valve is seeing an acceleration error
there is an error in the system
the gyro drift is being corrected normally
cards.explain: A deflection that lasts, rather than one that fluctuates, means a system error.

cards.question: Why can the compass rose of the ADF RMI show any heading immediately on power up
options: the direction taken up by the gyro after run-up may be any direction
the slaving annunciator is held at zero during the whole run-up
the flux valve needs several minutes before it delivers any signal
cards.explain: The rose follows the gyro, and the gyro runs up pointing anywhere.

cards.question: The system has just been switched on and the heading shown is wrong. Why does it take time to become correct?
options: the compass rose motor is deliberately damped during the run-up
the slaving torque motor may move the gyro by only 2° per minute
the flux valve must first warm up before it delivers its excitation
cards.explain: A large initial error can only be worked off at the slow torquing rate.

cards.question: A pilot uses the synchronizing knob shortly after start up. What is the effect?
options: the time until the heading indication is correct becomes much shorter
the torquing rate of the gyro is raised to 700° per minute
the slaving annunciator is switched off for the rest of the flight
cards.explain: Minimising the difference by hand saves the slow automatic torquing.

cards.question: Why is the flux valve signal coupled with the gyro heading instead of being sent straight to the indicator
options: it can fluctuate wildly for a short time under the influence of acceleration
it is far too weak to drive the compass rose motor of the indicator
it is a three-phase signal which the compass card cannot accept at all
cards.explain: Acceleration makes the raw valve signal jump about, so the gyro steadies it.

cards.question: Which kind of stability is supplied by each unit of a remote compass with ADF/RMI
options: long-term stability from the gyro, short-term from the flux valve
long-term stability from the flux valve, short-term from the gyro
long-term stability from the coupler, short-term from the gyro
cards.explain: The valve holds the long term truth, the gyro the short term steadiness.

cards.question: An aircraft accelerates on take off and then cruises for hours. Which unit takes out which error?
options: the coupler takes out the acceleration errors and the valve the drift
the valve takes out the acceleration errors and the gyro the drift
the gyro takes out the acceleration errors and the valve the drift
cards.explain: The gyro covers the short acceleration errors, the flux valve the slow drift.

cards.question: An engineer does not want to wait for the automatic alignment. How is the stator of the control transformer adjusted?
options: by holding the mode switch in the SLAVED position
by depressing and rotating the synchronisation knob
by depressing and rotating the course selector knob
cards.explain: The stator is set by hand with the synchronisation knob.

cards.question: Which errors are offset by the two precision potentiometers of the remote compensator
options: the A and B errors
the A error alone
the B and C errors
cards.explain: The N − S and E − W settings together deal with the B and C errors.

cards.question: A flux valve is indexed, that is prefixed. What does this mean when the A error is to be compensated?
options: it must be twisted until the B error is also at zero
it must not be twisted in its mounting
it must be twisted only with the compensator switched off
cards.explain: An indexed valve is not allowed to be turned, so that way of taking out the A error is barred.

cards.question: What makes it unnecessary to update the gyro by torquing in a system with a compass coupler
options: the differences are balanced out by a differential synchro
the gyro used in such a system has no drift to be corrected
the flux valve signal is passed to the indicator on its own
cards.explain: Because the coupler itself removes the difference, the gyro need not be torqued.

cards.question: What becomes of the two signals in the coupler when the DG mode is selected
options: the heading signal is switched off, the valve signal still passes through
the heading signal still passes through, the valve signal is amplified more
the heading signal still passes through, the valve signal is switched off
cards.explain: Only the flux valve signal is cut; the heading still runs through the coupler.

cards.question: The flux valve fails during flight. Which mode of operation has to be used?
options: the fast synchronisation mode
the DG mode
the slaved mode
cards.explain: With no usable valve signal the system has to run on the gyro alone, which is DG mode.

cards.question: The system has been in DG mode for a long time and the heading has slowly wandered. What must the crew do?
options: switch briefly to the slaved mode and straight back again
wait for the synchronising annunciator to null it out
correct the indication with the SET HDG knob
cards.explain: In DG mode nothing corrects the drift automatically, so it is set out by hand.

cards.question: A remote compass system is found in which the gyro is never torqued. Which arrangement must it have?
options: a coupler in which a differential synchro balances the signals
an indicator in which a control transformer balances the signals
a coupler in which a torque motor balances the signals
cards.explain: Only the coupler arrangement with a differential synchro removes the need to torque the gyro.

cards.question: Fast synchronisation has been running for well over its minimum time. What else must happen before it is complete?
options: the synchronisation error must have come down to 2° or less
the synchronising annunciator must have been off for 2 minutes
the synchronisation error must have come down to 2° per minute
cards.explain: Both the time and an error within two degrees are needed before it finishes.

cards.question: Which state of the fast synchronisation is required for the superflag signal to appear
options: fast synchronisation must have been run at least once
fast synchronisation must not be in operation
fast synchronisation must be in operation at the time
cards.explain: One of the listed conditions for the superflag is that fast synchronisation is not running.

cards.question: Which two conditions concerning the gyro and the servo circuit must hold for the superflag signal to appear
options: the DG or INS is valid and the servo circuit is nulled out
the DG is in free azimuth and the servo circuit is complete
the DG or INS is valid and the servo circuit is complete
cards.explain: Validity of the gyro or INS and a complete servo circuit are two of the listed conditions.

cards.question: The maintenance monitor responded only briefly during a flight. What does that mean for the compass system?
options: its functioning is not affected
its heading output must be treated as invalid
it must be put into the DG mode for the rest of the flight
cards.explain: A temporary response has no effect on how the system works.

cards.question: A compass system is switched off for half a minute and then switched on again in SLAVED. Does fast synchronisation run?
options: no, the switch-off pause was too short for it
yes, every switch-on in SLAVED will start it
no, it runs only when the mode is left in DG
cards.explain: A pause of about two minutes is needed, so half a minute does not trigger the logic.

cards.question: What shows the pilot that the signal from his compass system is not valid
options: a heading warning flag
the synchronising annunciator
the compass superflag
cards.explain: Loss of validity is shown by the heading warning flag.

cards.question: What does the abbreviation HSI stand for
options: Horizontal Situation Indicator
Heading and Situation Instrument
Horizontal Stabiliser Indicator
cards.explain: HSI is the Horizontal Situation Indicator.

cards.question: A pilot glances at the HSI for his heading. Which indication on it is the main one?
options: the distance readout
the course bar
the compass rose
cards.explain: The compass rose is the HSI's main indication.

cards.question: A pilot reads the heading on the ND in front of him. Which compass system supplies it?
options: the opposite compass system
their own compass system
whichever system the transfer switch selects
cards.explain: The HSI or ND is fed by the compass system of its own side.

cards.question: Which compass system do the RMIs show
options: the system feeding the autoflight computer
the opposite compass system
their own compass system
cards.explain: The RMI deliberately carries the heading of the other side's system.

cards.question: To which autoflight system is the heading of compass system 1 provided
options: to autoflight system number 1
to autoflight system number 2
to both autoflight systems together
cards.explain: The autoflight systems are fed straight across, one for one.

cards.question: To what besides the other heading sensor can the heading transfer switch connect a user
options: to a third unit if one is available
to the flux valve signal taken on its own
to the autoflight system of the other side
cards.explain: Where a third unit exists the transfer switch can reach it too.

cards.question: A heading leaves the compass coupler on its way to the HSIs. Which heading is it?
options: the uncorrected flux valve heading
the gyro supported magnetic heading
the free azimuth platform heading
cards.explain: What leaves the coupler is the magnetic heading after the gyro has steadied it.

cards.question: To which compass system is the flight recorder normally switched
options: to compass system 1
to both systems in turn
to compass system 2
cards.explain: The flight recorder normally sits on compass system 2.

cards.question: How are the ADF RMIs normally switched to the two compass systems?
options: straight, each to its own system
crosswise, each to the opposite system
both to the same system
cards.explain: The ADF RMIs are fed across, each from the other side's system.

cards.question: From which viewpoint does the HSI present the situation of the aircraft
options: as seen from behind
as seen from above
as seen from the side
cards.explain: The HSI gives a plan view, the aircraft seen from above.

cards.question: To which kind of ground station is the course selected on an HSI related
options: an ADF broadcast station
a VOR ground radio station
a DME ground station
cards.explain: The selectable course on the HSI belongs to a VOR station.

cards.question: The white bar on an HSI has moved away from the centre. What is it telling the crew?
options: there is a deviation from the selected heading
there is a deviation from the selected course
there is a deviation in the distance to the station
cards.explain: The bar is the course deviation indication of the HSI.

cards.question: What can the HSI show with respect to a DME ground station
options: the bearing to it
the distance to it
the deviation from it
cards.explain: From a DME station the HSI takes the distance.

cards.question: Which kind of system do all the further indications on an HSI belong to
options: autoflight systems
navigation systems
attitude reference systems
cards.explain: Every extra indication on the HSI is a navigation system indication.

cards.question: A pilot compares the heading on the ND with the heading on the RMI in front of him. Which sources is he comparing?
options: the opposite compass system against the flight recorder
his own compass system against the autoflight system
his own compass system against the opposite one
cards.explain: Because the two displays are fed from opposite systems, the comparison is a cross check of both.

cards.question: A heading warning flag has appeared on one side, so what can the pilot do about it?
options: use the compass controller to take the free azimuth heading instead
use the synchronizing knob to re-set the compass rose by hand
use the heading transfer switch to take the other heading sensor
cards.explain: The transfer switch is the way of getting a valid heading back.

cards.question: An HSI loses its heading while the RMI beside it still shows one. Which compass system has gone?
options: the one selected with the heading transfer switch
the one belonging to that side of the cockpit
the one belonging to the opposite side of the cockpit
cards.explain: The HSI is fed by its own system and the RMI by the other one, so the failure is on its own side.

cards.question: One of the two compass systems fails in flight. What happens to the consumers that were fed by it?
options: they can all be switched to the system that is still working
they are fed directly from the flux valve of the failed system
they hold the last valid heading until the system is reset
cards.explain: Every affected consumer can be moved over to the surviving system.

cards.question: What is achieved by exciting the synchros from various voltage sources
options: a receiver is always on a transmitting synchro fed by its own bus
a receiver is always fed from two independent buses at the same time
a receiver is always supplied even when the coupler itself has failed
cards.explain: Spreading the excitation keeps each receiver and its synchro on a common bus.

cards.question: An HSI shows several indications driven from different sources. Which one of them is driven by the heading system?
options: the compass rose
the course bar
the distance
cards.explain: The rose is the heading indication; the course bar and the distance are navigation system indications.

cards.question: What is meant by a glass cockpit
options: the instrument glasses are replaced by a scratch free type
computers and displays are used instead of instruments
the instruments are fitted behind one large glass panel
cards.explain: Glass cockpit means instruments have given way to computers and displays.

cards.question: What is the system used for flight monitoring in a glass cockpit called in many aircraft
options: EFIS
CDS
EIS
cards.explain: The flight monitoring displays are commonly called EFIS.

cards.question: Which three items are the components of a typical electronic instrument system
options: Display units, control panels and pressure sensors
Display computers, display units and control panels
Display computers, control panels and warning horns
cards.explain: The three listed components are the display computers, the display units and the control panels.

cards.question: A system is fitted with as few display computers as it is allowed to have, so how many is that?
options: Three
Four
Two
cards.explain: There are at least two display computers, and large aircraft have a third for redundancy.

cards.question: How many indication display screens does the display system have in the cockpit
options: Eight
Six
Four
cards.explain: The cockpit carries six indication display screens.

cards.question: What do the letters ECAM stand for
options: Electronic centralized aircraft monitor
Electronic central alert monitor
Engine centralized aircraft monitor
cards.explain: ECAM is the electronic centralized aircraft monitor.

cards.question: How many display management computers are installed and what do they do with the data they receive
options: Three computers, forwarding the data to the display units
Two computers, forwarding the data to the display units
Three computers, forwarding the data to the warning computers
cards.explain: Three identical display management computers take in the data and pass it to the display units.

cards.question: An engineer counts the flight warning computers of the system, so how many does he find?
options: One
Three
Two
cards.explain: Two identical flight warning computers are fitted.

cards.question: A crew is flying an aircraft with a glass cockpit. How is their flight monitoring done?
options: by one display for each pilot
by two displays for each pilot
by two displays shared by both pilots
cards.explain: Each pilot has two displays for flight monitoring.

cards.question: Where are the many engine parameters shown in a glass cockpit
options: on the related engine control panel
on two displays for each pilot
on two central displays
cards.explain: Engine parameters go on the two central displays.

cards.question: Where are the alerts of the central warning panel presented in a glass cockpit
options: at the related control panel
in a display
on a printed caption board
cards.explain: Those alerts move from the panel onto a display.

cards.question: The engine data and the auto flight system data both reach a display computer, so in which form do they arrive?
options: One is digital and one is analogue
Both are analogue
Both are digital
cards.explain: Navigation, auto flight and engine inputs are all listed as digital.

cards.question: Why does a large aircraft carry a third display computer
options: To drive the control panels
For redundancy
To convert analogue inputs
cards.explain: The third computer is fitted on large aircraft for redundancy.

cards.question: How does the electronic flight instrument system stand in relation to the electronic instrument system
options: It is a part of it and shows navigation data
It is a separate system and shows engine data
It replaces it and shows alert messages
cards.explain: EFIS is part of the EIS and its job is to show navigation data.

cards.question: How many control panels serve the centre displays and what is selected on them
options: One panel, used to select the computer to be monitored
One panel, used to select the system to be monitored
Two panels, used to select the system to be monitored
cards.explain: A single control panel serves the centre displays and selects the system to be monitored.

cards.question: Which further information is presented on the electronic instruments besides the navigation data
options: The limits of the engine parameters
The condition of the air conditioning system
The activities of the auto flight system
cards.explain: The electronic flight instruments also show what the auto flight system is doing.

cards.question: How are the six indication display screens divided between the electronic flight instruments and the central monitoring displays
options: Two flight instrument displays and four monitoring displays
Three flight instrument displays and three monitoring displays
Four flight instrument displays and two monitoring displays
cards.explain: Four of the six are flight instrument displays and two are central monitoring displays.

cards.question: Which two displays make up the centralized monitoring pair on an Airbus aircraft
options: The primary flight display and the system display
The engine and warning display and the system display
The engine and warning display and the navigation display
cards.explain: The pair is the engine and warning display together with the system display.

cards.question: Which of the two EICAS displays on a Boeing aircraft carries the engine and warning indications
options: The upper EICAS display
The lower EICAS display
The auxiliary EICAS display
cards.explain: The upper EICAS is the engine and warning display and the auxiliary one is the system display.

cards.question: Which kind of information does the primary flight display supply
options: Flight planning information and parameters
Engine monitoring information and parameters
Flight monitoring information and parameters
cards.explain: The primary flight display is the flight monitoring display.

cards.question: Which of these parameters does the primary flight display supply?
options: Total air temperature
Gross weight
Radio altitude
cards.explain: Radio altitude is one of the parameters listed for the primary flight display; total air temperature and gross weight are carried on the engine and system displays instead.

cards.question: Which annunciation does the primary flight display supply
options: The engine mode annunciation
The flight phase annunciation
The flight mode annunciation
cards.explain: The flight mode annunciation is one of the listed primary flight display parameters.

cards.question: With respect to which plane does the navigation display present the situation of the aircraft
options: The horizontal plane with respect to the flight path
The vertical plane with respect to the earth's surface
The horizontal plane with respect to the earth's surface
cards.explain: The navigation display works in the horizontal plane referred to the earth's surface.

cards.question: A flight warning computer works on the data it receives, so which three kinds of output does it generate?
options: Alert messages, aural alerts and synthetic voice
Alert messages, synthetic voice and engine parameters
Alert messages, aural alerts and system pages
cards.explain: The three outputs are the optical alert messages, the acoustic aural alerts and the voice announcements.

cards.question: An announcement in spoken words is heard in the cockpit, so which of the three warning outputs is this?
options: Synthetic voice
Aural alert
Alert message
